docs.title: Adding a Custom Block
docs.text:
This guide shows how to create an Enchanting Plus Table block with Anvil. It's written for Anvil beginners who already understand Minecraft concepts. Each step highlights what's necessary versus optional.

Every snippet on this page is taken from a project that compiles. Component arguments are keyword-only: write BlockDestructibleByMining(seconds_to_destroy=1.5), not BlockDestructibleByMining(1.5).

docs.title: Define the Block
docs.text:
blocks/enchanting_plus_table.py
from anvil.api.blocks.blocks import Block

# Namespace is inferred from anvilconfig; only provide the short name here.
def enchanting_plus_table():
    block = Block("enchanting_plus_table")
    return block

Warning

Declare a Block with a unique name (e.g., "enchanting_plus_table"). Namespace comes from anvilconfig.

docs.title: Server Description & States
docs.text:
server description
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel.enums import ItemCategory

# Show the block in the creative inventory (optional)
block.server.description.set_menu_category(ItemCategory.Construction)
block.server.description.add_state("is_awesome", (False, True))

Note

Server‑side states are optional. If you don't define any, the block still exports and works. A state name without a namespace gets the project's (tut:is_awesome). States, permutations and traits are covered in Block states, permutations and traits.

docs.title: Components — Visuals & Basics
docs.text:
components: visuals & basics
from anvil.api.blocks.components import (
    BlockCollisionBox,
    BlockDestructibleByMining,
    BlockGeometry,
    BlockMaterialInstance,
    BlockSelectionBox,
    InstanceSpec,
    InstanceVariant,
)

# Visuals (mandatory): geometry + at least one material instance
block.server.components.add(
    BlockCollisionBox(origin=(-8, 0, -8), size=(16, 12, 16)),
    BlockSelectionBox(origin=(-8, 0, -8), size=(16, 12, 16)),
    BlockMaterialInstance().add_instance(
        spec=InstanceSpec(
            blockbench="enchanting_plus_table",
            variations=[InstanceVariant(color="enchanting_plus_table")],
        )
    ),
    BlockGeometry(blockbench="enchanting_plus_table"),
    BlockDestructibleByMining(seconds_to_destroy=1.5),
)

Blockbench references

BlockGeometry(blockbench=...) and InstanceSpec(blockbench=...) name a Blockbench file under assets/bbmodels. Its model identifier must equal the file name, and the texture named in InstanceVariant(color=...) must exist inside that file. Mismatches raise an export error.

Blockbench collections

If your .bbmodel contains exported Blockbench collections, you can reference a specific part with BlockGeometry(blockbench="my_model", collection="bottom"). Anvil exports that collection as its own geometry and references it as geometry.<namespace>.my_model.bottom.

PBR Support

InstanceVariant takes the same arguments as TextureComponents: InstanceVariant(color="block", normal="block_normal", mer="block_mer") enables normal maps and metalness/emissive/roughness channels. See the PBR guide.

Display name

Anvil adds a BlockDisplayName for you, keyed tile.<namespace>:<name>.name in localization.csv. Add BlockDisplayName(value="Enchanting Plus Table") yourself only to override the generated text.

Failure

Visuals are mandatory. Without a BlockGeometry and at least one material instance, the block won't export.

docs.title: Block Sounds
docs.text:
block sounds
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel.enums import BlockSoundGroup

block.client.sound_group(BlockSoundGroup.Wood)

Note

A sound group reuses the sounds of a vanilla block and needs no sound files. Custom block sounds are covered in Particles and sounds.

docs.title: Crafting Recipe
docs.text:
crafting
from anvil.api.items.crafting.shaped import ShapedCraftingRecipe
from anvil.api.vanilla.blocks import MinecraftBlockTypes
from anvil.api.vanilla.items import MinecraftItemTypes

recipe = ShapedCraftingRecipe(block.name)
recipe.result(block)
recipe.ingredients(
    [
        [
            MinecraftItemTypes.AmethystShard(),
            MinecraftBlockTypes.EnchantingTable(),
            MinecraftItemTypes.AmethystShard(),
        ],
        [
            MinecraftBlockTypes.GoldBlock(),
            MinecraftBlockTypes.GoldBlock(),
            MinecraftBlockTypes.GoldBlock(),
        ],
    ]
)
recipe.unlock_items([MinecraftBlockTypes.EnchantingTable()])
recipe.queue()

Note

Recipes are optional. If omitted, the block can still be obtained via creative inventory or commands. More recipe types are in Recipes and the item catalog.

docs.title: Block Item
docs.text:
block item
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel.enums import ItemCategory
from anvil.api.items.components import ItemIcon, ItemMaxStackSize
from anvil.api.pbr.texture_set import TextureComponents

item = block.item
item.server.description.set_menu_category(ItemCategory.Construction)
item.server.components.add(
    ItemMaxStackSize(value=64),
    ItemIcon(textures=TextureComponents(color=item.name)),
)

Tip

The block's item is available as block.item. Accessing it creates an Item with the block's name, and block.queue() queues it too. The icon is read from assets/textures/items/enchanting_plus_table.png. Add ItemBlockPlacer(block=block) when the item should place the block itself instead of relying on the game's default block item.

docs.title: Queue the Block
docs.text:
finalize
block.queue()
return block

Success

Queuing is mandatory. If you don't call block.queue(), the framework will not export the block. Queuing the block also queues its client file and its item.

docs.title: Full Example — Enchanting Plus Table
docs.text:
blocks/enchanting_plus_table.py
from anvil.api.blocks.blocks import Block
from anvil.api.blocks.components import (
    BlockCollisionBox,
    BlockDestructibleByMining,
    BlockGeometry,
    BlockMaterialInstance,
    BlockSelectionBox,
    InstanceSpec,
    InstanceVariant,
)
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel.enums import BlockSoundGroup, ItemCategory
from anvil.api.items.components import ItemIcon, ItemMaxStackSize
from anvil.api.items.crafting.shaped import ShapedCraftingRecipe
from anvil.api.pbr.texture_set import TextureComponents
from anvil.api.vanilla.blocks import MinecraftBlockTypes
from anvil.api.vanilla.items import MinecraftItemTypes


def enchanting_plus_table():
    block = Block("enchanting_plus_table")

    block.server.description.set_menu_category(ItemCategory.Construction)
    block.server.description.add_state("is_awesome", (False, True))

    # Visuals (mandatory)
    block.server.components.add(
        BlockCollisionBox(origin=(-8, 0, -8), size=(16, 12, 16)),
        BlockSelectionBox(origin=(-8, 0, -8), size=(16, 12, 16)),
        BlockMaterialInstance().add_instance(
            spec=InstanceSpec(
                blockbench="enchanting_plus_table",
                variations=[InstanceVariant(color="enchanting_plus_table")],
            )
        ),
        BlockGeometry(blockbench="enchanting_plus_table"),
        BlockDestructibleByMining(seconds_to_destroy=1.5),
    )
    block.client.sound_group(BlockSoundGroup.Wood)

    # Crafting recipe (optional)
    recipe = ShapedCraftingRecipe(block.name)
    recipe.result(block)
    recipe.ingredients(
        [
            [
                MinecraftItemTypes.AmethystShard(),
                MinecraftBlockTypes.EnchantingTable(),
                MinecraftItemTypes.AmethystShard(),
            ],
            [
                MinecraftBlockTypes.GoldBlock(),
                MinecraftBlockTypes.GoldBlock(),
                MinecraftBlockTypes.GoldBlock(),
            ],
        ]
    )
    recipe.unlock_items([MinecraftBlockTypes.EnchantingTable()])
    recipe.queue()

    # Block item (optional)
    item = block.item
    item.server.description.set_menu_category(ItemCategory.Construction)
    item.server.components.add(
        ItemMaxStackSize(value=64),
        ItemIcon(textures=TextureComponents(color=item.name)),
    )

    # Finalize (mandatory)
    block.queue()
    return block


EnchantingPlusTable = enchanting_plus_table()

docs.title: Custom Ticking
docs.text:
Use BlockTick to make your block run a tick custom component event periodically or randomly.

from anvil.api.blocks.components import BlockTick

block.server.components.add(BlockTick(interval_range=(10, 20), looping=True))

docs.title: Custom Components
docs.text:
For more complex logic, attach Custom Components. These are scripts that run in the game and can interact with the world.

from anvil.api.blocks.components import BlockCustomComponent


class MyBlockLogic(BlockCustomComponent):
    identifier = "my_block_logic"


block.server.components.add(MyBlockLogic())

See the Custom Components Guide for parameters and the TypeScript side.

docs.title: States, Permutations and Traits
docs.text: Make the block change with its state (a lit lantern, a rotated model) in Block states, permutations and traits.

docs.title: World Generation
docs.text: To make your block generate naturally in the world, see Generating features.

docs.title: Adding a Custom Camera
docs.text: This guide shows how to create a custom Camera Preset in Anvil. Camera presets allow you to define custom camera perspectives for players, useful for cutscenes, vehicles, or unique gameplay mechanics.

docs.title: Define the Camera
docs.text:
misc/my_camera.py
from anvil.api.camera import CameraPreset
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel.enums import CameraPresets

def register_my_camera():
    # 1. Create a preset inheriting from a base behavior
    camera = CameraPreset("my_custom_camera", CameraPresets.FollowOrbit)

    # 2. Configure properties
    camera.extend_player_rendering(True) # Render player model
    camera.radius(5.0) # Distance from target

    # 3. Queue for export
    camera.queue()

docs.title: Using the Camera
docs.text:
Once registered, you can activate this camera using the /camera command or script API.

# The namespace is defined in your anvilconfig.json
/camera @s set <namespace>:my_custom_camera

docs.title: Adding a Custom Entity
docs.text:
This tutorial walks you through creating a compact Redstone Golem entity with Anvil. It targets Anvil beginners who already understand Minecraft concepts. Each step explicitly marks what's necessary and what's optional.

Every snippet on this page is taken from a project that compiles. Component arguments are keyword-only: write EntityHealth(value=20), not EntityHealth(20).

docs.title: Define the Entity
docs.text:
entities/redstone_golem.py
from anvil.api.actors.entity import Entity

# Namespace is inferred from anvilconfig; only provide the short name here.
def redstone_golem():
    entity = Entity("redstone_golem")
    return entity

Warning

Declare an Entity with a unique name (e.g., "redstone_golem"). The namespace comes from anvilconfig.

Export rule

You must queue the entity later with entity.queue(...). If you skip this, the framework will not export the entity.

docs.title: Client Description
docs.text:
client visuals
from anvil.api.pbr.texture_set import TextureComponents

# Both names point to assets/bbmodels/redstone_golem.bbmodel and a texture inside it.
entity.client.description.add_geometry("redstone_golem")
entity.client.description.add_texture(
    blockbench="redstone_golem",
    component=TextureComponents(color="redstone_golem"),
)

Blockbench references

The first argument of description.add_geometry, description.texture and description.animation names a Blockbench file under assets/bbmodels. The model identifier, texture names and animation names inside that file must match what you reference, or Anvil raises an error at build time.

PBR Support

Add PBR maps that are also stored in the Blockbench file: TextureComponents(color="redstone_golem", normal="redstone_golem_normal", mer="redstone_golem_mer"). See the PBR guide.

Material defaults

Anvil adds a default material named entity_alphatest. Add others with description.add_material(name, material).

Failure

Visuals are mandatory. Without a geometry and a texture on the client description, nothing is renderable.

What if I want an invisible entity?

Use entity.client.description.set_dummy() for a non‑rendered, logic‑only entity.

docs.title: Render Controller
docs.text:
render controller
rc = entity.client.description.render_controller("default")
rc.set_geometry("redstone_golem")
rc.add_texture("redstone_golem")

Warning

A render controller is required for the model to appear in‑game. The names you pass are the short names you registered on the description.

Optional tuning

Per‑part visibility, hurt and on‑fire colors, texture arrays and more are covered in Animating an entity.

docs.title: Server Components
docs.text:
server components
from anvil.api.actors.components import (
    EntityAILookAtPlayer,
    EntityAIRandomStroll,
    EntityCollisionBox,
    EntityHealth,
    EntityJumpStatic,
    EntityMovement,
    EntityMovementBasic,
    EntityNavigationWalk,
    EntityPhysics,
    EntityPushableByEntity,
    EntityTypeFamily,
)

entity.server.components.add(
    EntityCollisionBox(width=0.9, height=1.5),
    EntityPhysics(has_collision=True, has_gravity=True),
    EntityPushableByEntity(),
    EntityHealth(value=20, max=20),
    EntityTypeFamily(family=["golem", "mob"]),
    EntityMovement(value=0.25),
    EntityMovementBasic(),
    EntityNavigationWalk(),
    EntityJumpStatic(),
    EntityAIRandomStroll(priority=3),
    EntityAILookAtPlayer(priority=4),
)

Note

There are no minimum required server components. With none, the entity has no attributes (no collision, physics, etc.). Add components only for the behaviors you need. An option you leave out is omitted from the JSON, so the game default applies.

Walking needs four components

A mob only moves when it has a movement speed (EntityMovement), a movement type (EntityMovementBasic), a navigation (EntityNavigationWalk) and an AI goal that wants to go somewhere (EntityAIRandomStroll).

docs.title: Spawning
docs.text:
spawning
entity.server.description.config(is_spawnable=False)

Note

Entities are summonable (/summon namespace:redstone_golem) and spawnable (they get a spawn egg) by default. Use config(...) to change is_summonable, is_spawnable, is_experimental, runtime_identifier or spawn_category. Natural spawning is covered in Spawn rules and loot.

docs.title: Queue the Entity
docs.text:
finalize
entity.queue("misc")
return entity

Success

Queuing is mandatory. If you don't call entity.queue(...), the framework will not export the entity.

Queue groups

The argument to queue(...) is an export group. Anvil places generated files under <group>/. Choose any grouping string that fits your project layout. Call entity.set_display_name(name, spawn_egg_name) before queuing to name the entity and its egg; otherwise the name is the identifier in title case.

docs.title: Full Example — Redstone Golem
docs.text:
entities/redstone_golem.py
from anvil.api.actors.components import (
    EntityAILookAtPlayer,
    EntityAIRandomStroll,
    EntityCollisionBox,
    EntityHealth,
    EntityJumpStatic,
    EntityMovement,
    EntityMovementBasic,
    EntityNavigationWalk,
    EntityPhysics,
    EntityPushableByEntity,
    EntityTypeFamily,
)
from anvil.api.actors.entity import Entity
from anvil.api.pbr.texture_set import TextureComponents


def redstone_golem():
    entity = Entity("redstone_golem")

    # Client visuals (mandatory)
    entity.client.description.add_geometry("redstone_golem")
    entity.client.description.add_texture(
        blockbench="redstone_golem",
        component=TextureComponents(color="redstone_golem"),
    )

    # Render (mandatory)
    rc = entity.client.description.render_controller("default")
    rc.set_geometry("redstone_golem")
    rc.add_texture("redstone_golem")

    # Server (optional)
    entity.server.components.add(
        EntityCollisionBox(width=0.9, height=1.5),
        EntityPhysics(has_collision=True, has_gravity=True),
        EntityPushableByEntity(),
        EntityHealth(value=20, max=20),
        EntityTypeFamily(family=["golem", "mob"]),
        EntityMovement(value=0.25),
        EntityMovementBasic(),
        EntityNavigationWalk(),
        EntityJumpStatic(),
        EntityAIRandomStroll(priority=3),
        EntityAILookAtPlayer(priority=4),
    )

    entity.server.description.config(is_spawnable=False)

    # Finalize (mandatory)
    entity.queue("misc")
    return entity


RedstoneGolem = redstone_golem()

docs.title: Component Groups and Events
docs.text:
Component groups hold components that are only active after an event adds them. Events add and remove groups, trigger other events, run commands and more.

component groups and events
from anvil.api.actors.components import EntityHealth, EntityScale

# 1. Define component groups
entity.server.component_group("phase_1").add(EntityScale(value=1.0))
entity.server.component_group("phase_2").add(
    EntityScale(value=1.5), EntityHealth(value=100, max=100)
)

# 2. Define the transition event. Each `sequence` call adds one step.
phase_transition = entity.server.event("transform_to_phase_2")
phase_transition.add_sequence().add_component_groups(["phase_2"]).remove_component_groups(["phase_1"])
phase_transition.add_sequence().set_trigger("restore_health")

# 3. Run commands from an event
entity.server.event("restore_health").add_queue_command(["effect @s regeneration 5"])

# 4. Built-in events have their vanilla names
entity.server.event("minecraft:entity_spawned").add_component_groups(["phase_1"])

The event above exports as:

"transform_to_phase_2": {
  "sequence": [
    {"add": {"component_groups": ["phase_2"]}, "remove": {"component_groups": ["phase_1"]}},
    {"trigger": "restore_health"}
  ]
}

Note

Calling entity.server.event(name) twice returns the same event, so you can add to it from several places. Use event.add_randomize().set_weight(3).add_component_groups([...]) for weighted random picks, and entry.set_filters(Filter...) to make a sequence step conditional.

docs.title: Adding a Custom Item
docs.text:
This guide shows how to create an Arcane User Guide item with Anvil. It targets Anvil beginners who already understand Minecraft concepts. Each step highlights what's necessary versus optional.

Every snippet on this page is taken from a project that compiles. Component arguments are keyword-only: write ItemMaxStackSize(value=1), not ItemMaxStackSize(1).

docs.title: Define the Item
docs.text:
items/arcane_user_guide.py
from anvil.api.items.items import Item

# Namespace is inferred from anvilconfig; only provide the short name here.
def arcane_user_guide():
    item = Item("arcane_user_guide")
    return item

Warning

Declare an Item with a unique name (e.g., "arcane_user_guide"). Namespace comes from anvilconfig.

docs.title: Server Description
docs.text:
server description
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel.enums import ItemCategory

# Optional: where it appears in the creative inventory
item.server.description.set_menu_category(ItemCategory.Items)

Note

The category is optional. If omitted, the item still exports and can be obtained by commands or via recipes. set_menu_category also takes a group (an ItemGroups member or a catalog tag.<namespace>:<name> key) and is_hidden_in_commands.

docs.title: Components — Visuals & Basics
docs.text:
components: visuals & basics
from anvil.api.items.components import ItemDisplayName, ItemIcon, ItemMaxStackSize
from anvil.api.pbr.texture_set import TextureComponents

item.server.components.add(
    ItemIcon(textures=TextureComponents(color=item.name)),
    ItemDisplayName(value="Arcane User Guide"),
    ItemMaxStackSize(value=1),
)

Textures

ItemIcon(textures=TextureComponents(color=<name>)) reads assets/textures/items/<name>.png (here arcane_user_guide.png). If the texture doesn't exist, export fails.

PBR Support

Add PBR maps the same way: TextureComponents(color=item.name, normal="texture_normal", mer="texture_mer").

Localization

ItemDisplayName is optional: Anvil adds one keyed item.<namespace>:<name>.name when you leave it out. Every plain string passed to a display name becomes a localization key tracked in localization.csv. See Localization.

Failure

An item needs at least one component, or the export fails.

docs.title: Interactions
docs.text:
interactions
from anvil.api.items.components import ItemCooldown, ItemGlint, ItemUseModifiers

item.server.components.add(
    ItemCooldown(category=item.name, duration=1),  # separate cooldown channel per item name
    ItemUseModifiers(use_duration=700000, movement_modifier=0.4),
    ItemGlint(),  # cosmetic enchantment glint
)

Note

All of the above are optional. Use them to control usability and flair.

docs.title: Crafting Recipe
docs.text:
crafting
from anvil.api.items.crafting.shaped import ShapedCraftingRecipe
from anvil.api.vanilla.items import MinecraftItemTypes

recipe = ShapedCraftingRecipe(item.name)
recipe.result(item)
recipe.ingredients(
    [
        [MinecraftItemTypes.Book(), MinecraftItemTypes.Emerald()],
        [MinecraftItemTypes.LapisLazuli(), None],
    ]
)
recipe.queue()

Note

Recipes are optional. If omitted, the item is still available via category or commands. More recipe types are in Recipes and the item catalog.

docs.title: Item Client / Attachable (Optional)
docs.text:
item client
from anvil.api.logic.molang import Query
from anvil.api.pbr.texture_set import TextureComponents

client = item.client
client.description.add_geometry("arcane_user_guide")
client.description.add_texture(
    blockbench="arcane_user_guide",
    component=TextureComponents(color="arcane_user_guide"),
)
client.description.animation(
    "arcane_user_guide", "first_person", condition=Query.IsFirstPerson()
)
client.description.animation(
    "arcane_user_guide", "third_person", condition=~Query.IsFirstPerson()
)
rc = client.description.render_controller("default")
rc.set_geometry("arcane_user_guide")
rc.add_texture("arcane_user_guide")

Tip

The item's attachable is its client, available as item.client. Accessing it creates the attachable; it is only exported when you used it.

Same API as entities

From here, everything works exactly like the entity client: textures, materials, render controllers, animations, animation controllers, particles and sounds. See Animating an entity and, for armor, Wearables and attachables.

docs.title: Queue the Item
docs.text:
finalize
item.queue()
return item

Success

Queuing is mandatory. If you don't call item.queue(), the framework will not export the item. Queuing the item also queues its attachable, when one was created.

docs.title: Full Example — Arcane User Guide
docs.text:
items/arcane_user_guide.py
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel.enums import ItemCategory
from anvil.api.items.components import (
    ItemCooldown,
    ItemDisplayName,
    ItemGlint,
    ItemIcon,
    ItemMaxStackSize,
    ItemUseModifiers,
)
from anvil.api.items.crafting.shaped import ShapedCraftingRecipe
from anvil.api.items.items import Item
from anvil.api.logic.molang import Query
from anvil.api.pbr.texture_set import TextureComponents
from anvil.api.vanilla.items import MinecraftItemTypes


def arcane_user_guide():
    item = Item("arcane_user_guide")

    item.server.description.set_menu_category(ItemCategory.Items)

    # Visuals & basics (mandatory)
    item.server.components.add(
        ItemIcon(textures=TextureComponents(color=item.name)),
        ItemDisplayName(value="Arcane User Guide"),
        ItemMaxStackSize(value=1),
    )

    # Interactions (optional)
    item.server.components.add(
        ItemCooldown(category=item.name, duration=1),
        ItemUseModifiers(use_duration=700000, movement_modifier=0.4),
        ItemGlint(),
    )

    # Crafting recipe (optional)
    recipe = ShapedCraftingRecipe(item.name)
    recipe.result(item)
    recipe.ingredients(
        [
            [MinecraftItemTypes.Book(), MinecraftItemTypes.Emerald()],
            [MinecraftItemTypes.LapisLazuli(), None],
        ]
    )
    recipe.queue()

    # Item client / attachable (optional)
    client = item.client
    client.description.add_geometry("arcane_user_guide")
    client.description.add_texture(
        blockbench="arcane_user_guide",
        component=TextureComponents(color="arcane_user_guide"),
    )
    client.description.animation(
        "arcane_user_guide", "first_person", condition=Query.IsFirstPerson()
    )
    client.description.animation(
        "arcane_user_guide", "third_person", condition=~Query.IsFirstPerson()
    )
    rc = client.description.render_controller("default")
    rc.set_geometry("arcane_user_guide")
    rc.add_texture("arcane_user_guide")

    # Finalize (mandatory)
    item.queue()
    return item


ArcaneUserGuide = arcane_user_guide()

docs.title: Multi‑Variant Items (Leveraging Python)
docs.text:
items/enchanted_tomes.py
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel.enums import ItemCategory
from anvil.api.items.components import ItemDisplayName, ItemIcon, ItemMaxStackSize
from anvil.api.items.crafting.catalog import CraftingItemCatalog
from anvil.api.items.items import Item
from anvil.api.pbr.texture_set import TextureComponents


def enchanted_tomes():
    names = {"tome_air": "Tome of Air", "tome_fire": "Tome of Fire"}
    items = []
    for key, display in names.items():
        tome = Item(key)
        tome.server.description.set_menu_category(ItemCategory.Items)
        tome.server.components.add(
            ItemIcon(textures=TextureComponents(color=key)),
            ItemDisplayName(value=display),
            ItemMaxStackSize(value=1),
        )
        tome.queue()
        items.append(tome)

    # Optional: group in the creative catalog
    catalog = CraftingItemCatalog()
    catalog.add_group(ItemCategory.Items, "Enchanted Tomes", items[0], items)
    catalog.queue()
    return items


EnchantedTomes = enchanted_tomes()

Note

CraftingItemCatalog groups related items in the creative inventory. The third argument is the item or block whose icon the group shows. Entirely optional.

docs.title: Block States, Permutations and Traits
docs.text:
This tutorial builds a Brass Lantern that can be lit, faces the direction it was placed in, only sits on stone, and ticks. It shows how a block changes with its states, how permutations swap components, how traits give the game-managed states, and how a custom component carries parameters to your scripts. Read Adding a Custom Block first.

The whole example compiles as written.

docs.title: States and Traits
docs.text:
blocks/brass_lantern.py
from anvil.api.blocks.blocks import Block
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel.enums import ItemCategory, ItemGroups, PlacementDirectionTrait

block = Block("brass_lantern")
description = block.server.description

description.set_menu_category(ItemCategory.Items, ItemGroups.Copper)
description.add_state("lit", (False, True))
description.traits.set_placement_direction(
    traits=[PlacementDirectionTrait.CardinalDirection]
)
  • add_state(name, values) declares a state you control (up to 16 values). The name gets the project namespace: tut:lit.
  • A trait adds states the game sets on placement. set_placement_direction gives minecraft:cardinal_direction (or facing_direction), set_placement_position gives block_face and vertical_half, set_connection the connection sides and set_multi_block(direction, part_count) the multi-block part.
"description": {
  "identifier": "tut:brass_lantern",
  "states": {"tut:lit": [false, true]},
  "menu_category": {"category": "items", "group": "minecraft:itemGroup.name.copper"},
  "traits": {"minecraft:placement_direction": {"enabled_states": ["minecraft:cardinal_direction"]}}
}

docs.title: Root Components
docs.text:
root components
from anvil.api.blocks.components import (
    BlockCollisionBox,
    BlockDestructibleByMining,
    BlockGeometry,
    BlockMaterialInstance,
    BlockPlacementFilter,
    BlockSelectionBox,
    BlockTick,
    InstanceSpec,
    InstanceVariant,
)
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel.enums import BlockFaceValues
from anvil.api.vanilla.blocks import MinecraftBlockTypes

block.server.components.add(
    BlockGeometry(blockbench="brass_lantern"),
    BlockMaterialInstance().add_instance(
        spec=InstanceSpec(
            blockbench="brass_lantern",
            variations=[InstanceVariant(color="brass_lantern")],
        )
    ),
    BlockCollisionBox(origin=(-4, 0, -4), size=(8, 10, 8)),
    BlockSelectionBox(origin=(-4, 0, -4), size=(8, 10, 8)),
    BlockDestructibleByMining(seconds_to_destroy=0.5),
    BlockPlacementFilter().add_condition(
        allowed_faces=[BlockFaceValues.Up],
        block_filter=[MinecraftBlockTypes.Stone(), MinecraftBlockTypes.Cobblestone()],
    ),
    BlockTick(interval_range=(40, 80), looping=True),
)

Note

BlockPlacementFilter limits where the block can be placed: here only on the top face of stone or cobblestone. BlockTick calls the onTick hook of the block's custom components every 40 to 80 ticks.

docs.title: Permutations
docs.text:
A permutation is a Molang condition and the components that apply while it is true. Components in a permutation replace the root component with the same identifier.

permutations
from anvil.api.blocks.components import BlockLightEmission
from anvil.api.logic.molang import Query

block.server.permutation(Query.BlockState("lit")).add(
    BlockLightEmission(value=12),
    BlockMaterialInstance().add_instance(
        spec=InstanceSpec(
            blockbench="brass_lantern",
            variations=[InstanceVariant(color="brass_lantern_lit")],
        )
    ),
)
block.server.permutation(
    Query.BlockState(PlacementDirectionTrait.CardinalDirection) == "north"
).add(BlockGeometry(blockbench="brass_lantern").set_n_way_visual_rotation(y="180"))

"permutations": [
  {
    "condition": "q.block_state('tut:lit')",
    "components": {
      "minecraft:light_emission": 12,
      "minecraft:material_instances": {"*": {"texture": "tut:brass_lantern_lit"}}
    }
  },
  {
    "condition": "(q.block_state('minecraft:cardinal_direction') == 'north')",
    "components": {
      "minecraft:geometry": {"n_way_visual_rotation": {"y": "180"}, "identifier": "geometry.tut.brass_lantern"}
    }
  }
]

State names in Molang

Query.BlockState("lit") resolves the bare name to the block's own state. Pass a trait enum member for the game's states.

Rotation without permutations

BlockGeometry(...).set_n_way_visual_rotation(y="q.block_state('minecraft:cardinal_direction') == 'north' ? 180 : 0") rotates the model from Molang, so one geometry component can replace four permutations.

docs.title: Custom Component With Parameters
docs.text:
Custom components carry data from Python to the Script API. Fields are declared like any dataclass field; Anvil validates them at export.

custom component
from typing import Annotated

from anvil.api.blocks.components import BlockCustomComponent
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel import InRange, json_field


class LanternToggle(BlockCustomComponent):
    identifier = "lantern_toggle"

    cooldown_ticks: Annotated[int, InRange(0, 200)] = json_field(default=10)


block.server.components.add(LanternToggle(cooldown_ticks=20))

"tut:lantern_toggle": {"cooldown_ticks": 20}

The TypeScript side reads params.cooldown_ticks in onPlayerInteract and sets the tut:lit state with block.setPermutation(block.permutation.withState("tut:lit", true)). See Custom Components.

docs.title: Sounds and the Item
docs.text:
sounds and item
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel.enums import BlockSoundGroup
from anvil.api.items.components import ItemBlockPlacer, ItemIcon
from anvil.api.pbr.texture_set import TextureComponents

block.client.sound_group(BlockSoundGroup.Chain)

item = block.item
item.server.description.set_menu_category(ItemCategory.Items, ItemGroups.Copper)
item.server.components.add(
    ItemIcon(textures=TextureComponents(color="brass_lantern")),
    ItemBlockPlacer(block=block, replace_block_item=True),
)

block.queue()

Note

ItemBlockPlacer(block=block, replace_block_item=True) makes the item the block's own item, so the icon from assets/textures/items/brass_lantern.png is what shows in the inventory.

docs.title: Full Example — Brass Lantern
docs.text:
blocks/brass_lantern.py
from typing import Annotated

from anvil.api.blocks.blocks import Block
from anvil.api.blocks.components import (
    BlockCollisionBox,
    BlockCustomComponent,
    BlockDestructibleByMining,
    BlockGeometry,
    BlockLightEmission,
    BlockMaterialInstance,
    BlockPlacementFilter,
    BlockSelectionBox,
    BlockTick,
    InstanceSpec,
    InstanceVariant,
)
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel.enums import (
    BlockFaceValues,
    BlockSoundGroup,
    ItemCategory,
    ItemGroups,
    PlacementDirectionTrait,
)
from anvil.api.items.components import ItemBlockPlacer, ItemIcon
from anvil.api.logic.molang import Query
from anvil.api.pbr.texture_set import TextureComponents
from anvil.api.vanilla.blocks import MinecraftBlockTypes
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel import InRange, json_field


class LanternToggle(BlockCustomComponent):
    identifier = "lantern_toggle"

    cooldown_ticks: Annotated[int, InRange(0, 200)] = json_field(default=10)


def brass_lantern():
    block = Block("brass_lantern")
    description = block.server.description

    description.set_menu_category(ItemCategory.Items, ItemGroups.Copper)
    description.add_state("lit", (False, True))
    description.traits.set_placement_direction(
        traits=[PlacementDirectionTrait.CardinalDirection]
    )

    block.server.components.add(
        BlockGeometry(blockbench="brass_lantern"),
        BlockMaterialInstance().add_instance(
            spec=InstanceSpec(
                blockbench="brass_lantern",
                variations=[InstanceVariant(color="brass_lantern")],
            )
        ),
        BlockCollisionBox(origin=(-4, 0, -4), size=(8, 10, 8)),
        BlockSelectionBox(origin=(-4, 0, -4), size=(8, 10, 8)),
        BlockDestructibleByMining(seconds_to_destroy=0.5),
        BlockPlacementFilter().add_condition(
            allowed_faces=[BlockFaceValues.Up],
            block_filter=[MinecraftBlockTypes.Stone(), MinecraftBlockTypes.Cobblestone()],
        ),
        BlockTick(interval_range=(40, 80), looping=True),
        LanternToggle(cooldown_ticks=20),
    )

    block.server.permutation(Query.BlockState("lit")).add(
        BlockLightEmission(value=12),
        BlockMaterialInstance().add_instance(
            spec=InstanceSpec(
                blockbench="brass_lantern",
                variations=[InstanceVariant(color="brass_lantern_lit")],
            )
        ),
    )
    block.server.permutation(
        Query.BlockState(PlacementDirectionTrait.CardinalDirection) == "north"
    ).add(BlockGeometry(blockbench="brass_lantern").set_n_way_visual_rotation(y="180"))

    block.client.sound_group(BlockSoundGroup.Chain)

    item = block.item
    item.server.description.set_menu_category(ItemCategory.Items, ItemGroups.Copper)
    item.server.components.add(
        ItemIcon(textures=TextureComponents(color="brass_lantern")),
        ItemBlockPlacer(block=block, replace_block_item=True),
    )

    block.queue()
    return block


BrassLantern = brass_lantern()

Blocks in other APIs

block.descriptor(lit=True) returns a BlockDescriptor with state values, accepted anywhere a vanilla MinecraftBlockTypes.X() is: loot tables, features, filters and recipes. To match blocks by tags only, write BlockDescriptor(tags=Query.AllTags(["stone"])).

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text:
Anvil exposes a Click-based command line interface through the anvil executable. Use anvil --help for the main command list and anvil <command> --help for command-specific usage.

This page documents the commands registered in src/anvil/cli.py and the behavior implemented by each command module.

docs.title: Command Overview
docs.text: Command Alias / implementation Project required Purpose init create No Scaffold a new Anvil project. build run Yes Build or export the configured project entry point. clean clear Yes Remove the current project's development packs. prof profile Yes Record a performance trace for the current project. process-sounds sounds No, but assets/sounds should exist Normalize and re-encode audio files in place. loopback lb No Enable Minecraft UWP loopback access and open the local test page.

docs.title: init / create
docs.text:
Scaffolds a new project and writes the base configuration, pack folders, and starter files. init is the primary command name; create is available as a direct alias.

anvil init <namespace> <project_name> [--preview] [--scriptapi] [--addon] [--vscode]
# or
anvil create <namespace> <project_name> [--preview] [--scriptapi] [--addon] [--vscode]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description namespace Project namespace. minecraft is reserved. project_name Project folder and package name.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Effect --preview Generate the project for Minecraft Preview com.mojang paths (Windows default export). --scriptapi Add Script API support, generate JavaScript scaffolding, and install the Script API npm dependencies. --addon Mark the project as an addon and apply addon-specific restrictions. --vscode Generate a VS Code workspace and launch it after scaffolding.

docs.title: Removed / Deprecated Options
docs.text:
The following flags were previously available on the initialization CLI command and have since been removed from the command-line interface:

Removed Option Status / Migration Details --pbr Configured in anvilconfig.json PBR functionality is configured in anvilconfig.json under [ANVIL] ("pbr": true / false) or used directly via the modular anvil.api.pbr submodules. --random_seed (formerly --seed) Configured in anvilconfig.json Random seed world generation is configured in anvilconfig.json under [ANVIL] ("random_seed": true / false). --fullns Removed Universal namespace formatting and validation are enforced automatically.

docs.title: What it creates
docs.text:
• anvilconfig.json with the project metadata and build settings.
  • A starter scripts/python/main.py entry point.
  • The project directories under assets/, scripts/, world/, marketing/, and output/.
  • .gitignore, CHANGELOG.md, and .github/workflows/release.yml.
  • When --scriptapi is enabled, package.json, tsconfig.json, esbuild.js, scripts/javascript/constants.ts, and scripts/javascript/main.ts are also created.
  • When --vscode is enabled, the project gets a .code-workspace file and a .vscode/launch.json file for debugging.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The command validates the namespace and project name before creating anything.
  • After scaffolding, the command switches into the new project directory and saves the generated config.
  • If --scriptapi is enabled, Anvil installs @minecraft/server, @minecraft/server-ui, @minecraft/vanilla-data, @starktma/minecraft-utils, and esbuild.

docs.title: run / build
docs.text:
Builds or exports the configured project entry point from anvilconfig.json with the current Python interpreter. Use anvil build in examples.

anvil build [--js-only] [--noarch] [--nocompile] [--mcaddon] [--mcworld] [--zip] [--tech-notes] [--workflow]

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Reads the entry point from anvilconfig.json.
  • Launches that entry point using the same interpreter that started anvil.
  • Appends any selected flags to the entry script unchanged.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Effect --js-only Forward a request to skip archive work where the entry point supports it. --noarch Forward a request to skip archive work where the entry point supports it. --nocompile Forward a request to skip compilation work where the entry point supports it. --mcaddon Forward a request to build a Minecraft addon package. --mcworld Forward a request to build a Minecraft world package. --zip Forward a request to build a ZIP archive. --tech-notes Forward a request to generate technical notes. --workflow Forward a request to refresh the GitHub workflow.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The command requires a valid anvilconfig.json in the current directory.
  • If the entry point is missing, Anvil prints a warning and exits without building.
  • The top-level CLI does not package files directly. It delegates the build logic to the project entry script.

docs.title: clean / clear
docs.text:
Deletes the current project's development packs from the matching com.mojang folders (Minecraft AppData on Windows, or output/com.mojang when using local export).

anvil clean

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Resolves the current project name and preview setting from anvilconfig.json.
  • Searches for the development resource pack and development behavior pack for that project.
  • Shows the detected paths and asks for confirmation before deleting anything.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• If no development packs are found, the command exits cleanly.
  • This command is useful when you want a clean export before the next build.

docs.title: prof / profile
docs.text:
Records a Speedscope-compatible performance trace for the current project.

anvil prof

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Reads the configured entry point from anvilconfig.json.
  • Runs py-spy record against the project entry point.
  • Writes the trace to output/anvil_trace.json.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• This command requires py-spy to be available on PATH.
  • If the project configuration is missing or incomplete, the command exits early with a warning.

docs.title: process-sounds / sounds
docs.text:
Batch processes audio files in assets/sounds, converts them to .ogg, and overwrites the originals.

anvil sounds [--target-lufs <value>] [--sample-rate <value>] [--quality <value>]

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Default Effect --target-lufs -18 Target loudness in LUFS. --sample-rate 32000 Output sample rate. --quality 0 Vorbis quality level.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Recursively walks assets/sounds.
  • Processes .wav, .mp3, and .ogg files.
  • Normalizes loudness, resamples the audio, and writes the result back as .ogg.
  • Prompts before starting because the operation overwrites source files.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• This command is destructive.
  • It requires ffmpeg to be installed and available on PATH.

docs.title: loopback / lb
docs.text:
Enables Minecraft UWP loopback access and opens the local loopback test page.

anvil lb

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Runs CheckNetIsolation LoopbackExempt -a -n="Microsoft.MinecraftUWP_8wekyb3d8bbwe".
  • Opens http://localhost:7003/ in the default browser.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• This command is specific to Windows and Minecraft UWP.
  • It is meant to remove the local network restriction that blocks loopback testing.

docs.title: Common Usage Patterns
docs.text:
anvil init my_ns awesome_project --scriptapi --vscode
anvil build --mcaddon
anvil clean
anvil sounds --target-lufs -16 --quality 2
anvil lb

docs.title: Practical Notes
docs.text:
• init (or create) can be run in an empty folder.
  • run, clean, and prof expect a valid Anvil project in the current directory.
  • process-sounds and clean can modify or delete files, so they prompt before doing work.
  • profile and process-sounds depend on external tools, not just Python packages.

docs.title: Understanding Your anvilconfig.json File
docs.text:
This is the canonical reference for anvilconfig.json. The overview pages link here instead of repeating the configuration tables.

The file defines the project name, namespace, versioning, and runtime flags that Anvil uses while generating packs and bundles.

docs.title: Sections
docs.text: The options are grouped by what they are used for. Each option must be in its section.

docs.title: [PACKAGE]
docs.text:
What the project is: its identity, names, descriptions and packaging target.

Key Type Description Default Restriction Can be Changed company str Company name used in the manifest.json authors section. Namespace None Yes namespace str Namespace for the project. namespace 1 to 8 lowercase letters, digits or _, starting with a letter. Not Advised project_name str Name of the project. my_project 1 to 16 lowercase letters, digits or _, starting with a letter. Not Advised display_name str Display name of the project. My Project None Yes project_description str Description used in localized text. My Project Packs None Yes behavior_description str Description of the behavior pack. My Project behavior Pack None Yes resource_description str Description of the resource pack. My Project Resource Pack None Yes target str Packaging target; can be world or addon. world None Yes

For an addon, the namespace must end with the initials of the project name, for example stark_mp for my_project. The initials also name the packs inside the Marketplace zip.

docs.title: [MANIFEST]
docs.text:
What the pack manifests carry: the release version and the UUIDs.

Key Type Description Default Restriction Can be Changed release str Version number of the project, used in manifest files. 1.0.0 X.X.X Yes rp_uuid list[UUIDv4] UUIDs of the resource packs. Randomly generated None Yes bp_uuid list[UUIDv4] UUIDs of the behavior packs. Randomly generated None Yes pack_uuid UUIDv4 UUID of the world template. Randomly generated None Yes data_module_uuid UUIDv4 UUID of the data module. Randomly generated None Yes resource_module_uuid UUIDv4 UUID of the resources module. Randomly generated None Yes script_module_uuid UUIDv4 UUID of the script module, when scriptapi is on. Randomly generated None Yes

docs.title: [FEATURES]
docs.text:
What the project's content uses.

Key Type Description Default Restriction Can be Changed scriptapi bool Enable/disable ScriptAPI support. false None Yes scriptui bool Enable/disable ScriptAPI/UI support. false None Yes pbr bool Enable/disable physically based rendering (PBR) support. false None Yes experimental bool Indicates if the project uses experimental features. false None Yes random_seed bool Enable/disable random seed support. false None Yes

docs.title: [BUILD]
docs.text:
How the project is built and exported. Debug output is turned on with the --debug build flag, not in this file.

Key Type Description Default Restriction Can be Changed preview bool Whether to generate the project for Minecraft release or preview versions. false None Yes entry_point str The main entry point script for the project. main.py None Yes js_bundle_script str The JavaScript bundle script for the project. node esbuild.js None Yes minify bool Whether to minify the JavaScript code and JSONs during the build process. false None Yes add_stamp bool Whether to add the Anvil header to generated files. true None Yes local_export bool Whether to export compiled behavior and resource packs to the local output/com.mojang folder. Defaults to false on Windows and true on non-Windows. false (Windows) / true (non-Windows) None Yes

docs.title: [ANVIL]
docs.text:
What Anvil records on its own. You don't need to edit it.

Key Type Description Default Restriction Can be Changed last_check str Last time Anvil checked @Mojang/bedrock-sample for updates. datetime None Not Advised vanilla_version str The latest Minecraft version Anvil found. 1.20.12 Automatically pulled from @Mojang/bedrock-sample. No

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
    "package": {
        "company": "StarkTMA",
        "namespace": "stark_mp",
        "project_name": "my_project",
        "display_name": "My Project",
        "project_description": "My Project Packs",
        "behavior_description": "My Project behavior Pack",
        "resource_description": "My Project Resource Pack",
        "target": "world"
    },
    "manifest": {
        "release": "1.0.0",
        "rp_uuid": ["00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"],
        "bp_uuid": ["00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"],
        "pack_uuid": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
        "data_module_uuid": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
        "resource_module_uuid": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
        "script_module_uuid": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
    },
    "features": {
        "scriptapi": true,
        "scriptui": true,
        "pbr": false,
        "experimental": false,
        "random_seed": false
    },
    "build": {
        "preview": false,
        "entry_point": "main.py",
        "js_bundle_script": "node esbuild.js",
        "minify": false,
        "add_stamp": true,
        "local_export": false
    },
    "anvil": {
        "last_check": "2024-01-16 19:06:58",
        "vanilla_version": "1.20.50.3"
    }
}

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The anvilconfig.json file is automatically generated when you run the anvil init (or anvil create) command. You can modify the file at any time, but be cautious—some changes might have unexpected results.
  • Project options that are not exposed as CLI flags during initialization (such as pbr and random_seed) are configured directly in this file under the features section.
  • Missing keys in the anvilconfig.json file will be automatically handled by Anvil during runtime.
  • You can add additional information to the anvilconfig.json file through the Anvil API. This is particularly useful for storing metadata not required during the project generation.

docs.title: Creating a Biome
docs.text:
This tutorial creates the Ember Fields, a hot overworld biome with its own terrain, colors, fog, sky, lighting and water. A biome has a server side (where and how it generates) and a client side (how it looks), and the client side points at the Vibrant Visuals settings files: fog, atmosphere, lighting and water.

Every snippet compiles as written. PBR must be enabled in anvilconfig.json for the lighting, atmosphere and water files.

docs.title: Server: Generation
docs.text:
worldgen/ember_fields.py
from anvil.api.biomes.biomes import Biome
from anvil.api.biomes.components import (
    BiomeClimate,
    BiomeMapTints,
    BiomeOverworldGenerationRules,
    BiomeOverworldHeight,
    BiomeSurfaceBuilder,
    BiomeTags,
)
from anvil.api.vanilla.biomes import MinecraftBiomeTags
from anvil.api.vanilla.blocks import MinecraftBlockTypes

biome = Biome("ember_fields")

biome.server.components.add(
    BiomeClimate(temperature=1.4, downfall=0.1),
    BiomeTags(
        tags=[MinecraftBiomeTags.Overworld, MinecraftBiomeTags.Monster, "ember_fields"]
    ),
    BiomeOverworldHeight(noise_params=(0.3, 0.4)),
    BiomeOverworldGenerationRules(generate_for_climates=[("warm", 2)]),
    BiomeSurfaceBuilder().set_overworld_builder(
        top_material=MinecraftBlockTypes.Basalt(),
        mid_material=MinecraftBlockTypes.Blackstone(),
        foundation_material=MinecraftBlockTypes.Deepslate(),
        sea_floor_material=MinecraftBlockTypes.Gravel(),
        sea_material=MinecraftBlockTypes.Water(),
    ),
    BiomeMapTints(foliage="#b35a2a").set_grass(tint="#c96b3a"),
)

"components": {
  "minecraft:climate": {"temperature": 1.4, "downfall": 0.1},
  "minecraft:tags": {"tags": ["overworld", "monster", "ember_fields"]},
  "minecraft:overworld_height": {"noise_params": [0.3, 0.4]},
  "minecraft:overworld_generation_rules": {"generate_for_climates": [["warm", 2]]},
  "minecraft:surface_builder": {"builder": {"type": "minecraft:overworld", "foundation_material": "minecraft:deepslate", "mid_material": "minecraft:blackstone", "top_material": "minecraft:basalt", "sea_floor_material": "minecraft:gravel", "sea_material": "minecraft:water"}},
  "minecraft:map_tints": {"foliage": "#b35a2a", "grass": {"tint": "#c96b3a"}}
}
  • BiomeTags is how everything else finds the biome: spawn rules, feature rules and structures filter on Filter.has_biome_tag("ember_fields"). Keep the vanilla tags the biome should still count as (Overworld, Monster, Animal...).
  • BiomeOverworldGenerationRules places the biome in the overworld climate bands; BiomeMultiNoiseGenerationRules is the alternative for custom dimensions.
  • The surface builder chooses the blocks; BiomeSurfaceMaterialAdjustments layers more blocks by height or noise.

Addons

A package of type addon cannot override a vanilla biome (Biome("plains", is_vanilla=True) raises). Custom biomes are fine.

docs.title: Vibrant Visuals Settings
docs.text:
The client biome references settings files by identifier. Build them first and pass the objects, so the identifiers never go out of sync.

visual settings
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel.enums import FogCameraLocation, RenderDistanceType
from anvil.api.pbr.atmosphere import AtmosphericSettings
from anvil.api.pbr.fog import FogSettings
from anvil.api.pbr.lighting import LightingSettings, LocalLighting
from anvil.api.pbr.water import WaterSettings

fog = FogSettings("ember_fog")
fog.add_distance_location("#c9663a", 8, 96, RenderDistanceType.Fixed)
fog.add_distance_location(
    "#3b1a0e", 0, 12, RenderDistanceType.Fixed, FogCameraLocation.Water
)
fog.air_density(0.25, zero_density_height=120, max_density_height=60)
fog.queue()

sky = AtmosphericSettings("ember_sky")
sky.sky_zenith_color([(0.0, "#7a2a14"), (0.5, "#ff9a4d"), (1.0, "#7a2a14")])
sky.sky_horizon_color("#ffb070")
sky.sun_glare_shape(0.6)
sky.queue()

light = LightingSettings("ember_lighting")
light.orbital_lights(sun_illuminance=80000, sun_color="#ffc078", moon_illuminance=0.4)
light.ambient(4, "#ff8040")
light.emissive(0.2)
light.queue()

water = WaterSettings("ember_water")
water.particle_concentrations(cdom=2.0, chlorophyll=0.1, suspended_sediment=40)
water.waves(enabled=True, depth=0.3, frequency=0.8)
water.queue()

lights = LocalLighting()
lights.add_point_light("tut:brass_lantern", "#ffb347")
lights.queue()

Keyframes

Any value that can change over the day takes a list of (time, value) tuples with time from 0 (midnight) to 1, or a single value for a constant.

Colors

Colors are hex strings ("#ff8040"), (r, g, b) floats from 0 to 1 or (r, g, b) integers from 0 to 255, with an optional alpha. They are written as hex.

docs.title: Client: Appearance
docs.text:
client biome
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel.enums import MusicCategory

client = biome.client
client.sky_color("#e07a3f")
client.fog_appearance(fog)
client.atmosphere_identifier(sky)
client.lighting_identifier(light)
client.water_identifier(water)
client.grass_appearance("#c96b3a")
client.foliage_appearance("#b35a2a")
client.water_appearance("#5a2b14", surface_opacity=0.9)
client.precipitation(ash=0.4)
client.biome_music(music_definition=MusicCategory.Soulsand_valley, volume_multiplier=0.6)

biome.queue()

"minecraft:client_biome": {
  "description": {"identifier": "tut:ember_fields"},
  "components": {
    "minecraft:sky_color": {"sky_color": "#e07a3f"},
    "minecraft:fog_appearance": {"fog_identifier": "tut:ember_fog"},
    "minecraft:atmosphere_identifier": {"atmosphere_identifier": "tut:ember_sky"},
    "minecraft:lighting_identifier": {"lighting_identifier": "tut:ember_lighting"},
    "minecraft:water_identifier": {"water_identifier": "tut:ember_water"},
    "minecraft:grass_appearance": {"color": "#c96b3a"},
    "minecraft:foliage_appearance": {"color": "#b35a2a"},
    "minecraft:water_appearance": {"surface_color": "#5a2b14", "surface_opacity": 0.9},
    "minecraft:precipitation": {"ash": 0.4},
    "minecraft:biome_music": {"music_definition": "soulsand_valley", "volume_multiplier": 0.6}
  }
}
  • The builders on biome.client add the client components for you; biome.client.components.add(BiomeClientSkyColor(...)) is the same thing spelled out.
  • grass_appearance and foliage_appearance also accept a vanilla color map name such as "swamp_grass".
  • ambient_sounds(addition=, loop=, mood=) returns sound definitions to add .ogg files to, exactly like sound definitions.

Only the sides you use

biome.queue() exports the server file and the client file only when you touched them. A biome used for a feature filter alone needs neither.

docs.title: Full Example — Ember Fields
docs.text:
worldgen/ember_fields.py
from anvil.api.biomes.biomes import Biome
from anvil.api.biomes.components import (
    BiomeClimate,
    BiomeMapTints,
    BiomeOverworldGenerationRules,
    BiomeOverworldHeight,
    BiomeSurfaceBuilder,
    BiomeTags,
)
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel.enums import FogCameraLocation, MusicCategory, RenderDistanceType
from anvil.api.pbr.atmosphere import AtmosphericSettings
from anvil.api.pbr.fog import FogSettings
from anvil.api.pbr.lighting import LightingSettings, LocalLighting
from anvil.api.pbr.water import WaterSettings
from anvil.api.vanilla.biomes import MinecraftBiomeTags
from anvil.api.vanilla.blocks import MinecraftBlockTypes


def ember_visuals():
    fog = FogSettings("ember_fog")
    fog.add_distance_location("#c9663a", 8, 96, RenderDistanceType.Fixed)
    fog.add_distance_location(
        "#3b1a0e", 0, 12, RenderDistanceType.Fixed, FogCameraLocation.Water
    )
    fog.air_density(0.25, zero_density_height=120, max_density_height=60)
    fog.queue()

    sky = AtmosphericSettings("ember_sky")
    sky.sky_zenith_color([(0.0, "#7a2a14"), (0.5, "#ff9a4d"), (1.0, "#7a2a14")])
    sky.sky_horizon_color("#ffb070")
    sky.sun_glare_shape(0.6)
    sky.queue()

    light = LightingSettings("ember_lighting")
    light.orbital_lights(sun_illuminance=80000, sun_color="#ffc078", moon_illuminance=0.4)
    light.ambient(4, "#ff8040")
    light.emissive(0.2)
    light.queue()

    water = WaterSettings("ember_water")
    water.particle_concentrations(cdom=2.0, chlorophyll=0.1, suspended_sediment=40)
    water.waves(enabled=True, depth=0.3, frequency=0.8)
    water.queue()

    lights = LocalLighting()
    lights.add_point_light("tut:brass_lantern", "#ffb347")
    lights.queue()
    return fog, sky, light, water


def ember_fields():
    fog, sky, light, water = ember_visuals()
    biome = Biome("ember_fields")

    biome.server.components.add(
        BiomeClimate(temperature=1.4, downfall=0.1),
        BiomeTags(
            tags=[MinecraftBiomeTags.Overworld, MinecraftBiomeTags.Monster, "ember_fields"]
        ),
        BiomeOverworldHeight(noise_params=(0.3, 0.4)),
        BiomeOverworldGenerationRules(generate_for_climates=[("warm", 2)]),
        BiomeSurfaceBuilder().set_overworld_builder(
            top_material=MinecraftBlockTypes.Basalt(),
            mid_material=MinecraftBlockTypes.Blackstone(),
            foundation_material=MinecraftBlockTypes.Deepslate(),
            sea_floor_material=MinecraftBlockTypes.Gravel(),
            sea_material=MinecraftBlockTypes.Water(),
        ),
        BiomeMapTints(foliage="#b35a2a").set_grass(tint="#c96b3a"),
    )

    client = biome.client
    client.sky_color("#e07a3f")
    client.fog_appearance(fog)
    client.atmosphere_identifier(sky)
    client.lighting_identifier(light)
    client.water_identifier(water)
    client.grass_appearance("#c96b3a")
    client.foliage_appearance("#b35a2a")
    client.water_appearance("#5a2b14", surface_opacity=0.9)
    client.precipitation(ash=0.4)
    client.biome_music(music_definition=MusicCategory.Soulsand_valley, volume_multiplier=0.6)

    return biome.queue()


EmberFields = ember_fields()

Fill the biome with ores, lanterns and trees in Generating features.

docs.title: Custom Components Guide
docs.text: Custom Components allow you to run custom Logic in your blocks and items using the Minecraft Script API. This guide explains how to use them in Anvil, following a modular pattern.

docs.title: 1. Defining the Component in Python
docs.text:
Define your own component class by subclassing BlockCustomComponent or ItemCustomComponent. A component is a dataclass: set its identifier and declare its parameters as fields with json_field. Don't write an __init__.

The identifier is in your project namespace. A bare name such as "my_block_logic" becomes <namespace>:my_block_logic.

docs.title: Block Component
docs.text:
from anvil.api.blocks.components import BlockCustomComponent
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel import json_field

class MyBlockLogic(BlockCustomComponent):
    identifier = "my_block_logic"

# Usage in your block definition
block.server.components.add(MyBlockLogic())

docs.title: Item Component
docs.text:
from anvil.api.items.components import ItemCustomComponent
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel import json_field

class MyItemLogic(ItemCustomComponent):
    identifier = "my_item_logic"

# Usage in your item definition
item.server.components.add(MyItemLogic())

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Each field is a parameter your script reads. The annotation says what the field accepts, and Anvil checks it when the pack is exported. Bounds and JSON shapes go in Annotated, after the real type, so the field still shows exactly what to pass:

from typing import Annotated

from anvil.api.blocks.components import BlockCustomComponent
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel.types import RGB, RGB255, RGBA, RGBA255, HexRGB, HexRGBA
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel import Hex, InRange, MinMax, json_field

class GravityWell(BlockCustomComponent):
    identifier = "gravity_well"

    pull: Annotated[float, InRange(0, 10)] = json_field()
    delay: Annotated[float | tuple[float, float], MinMax] = json_field(default=1)
    color: Annotated[HexRGB | HexRGBA | RGB | RGBA | RGB255 | RGBA255, Hex] | None = json_field(
        default=None
    )

block.server.components.add(GravityWell(pull=4, delay=(1, 3), color=(255, 0, 0)))
# {"<namespace>:gravity_well": {"pull": 4, "delay": {"min": 1, "max": 3}, "color": "#ff0000"}}

A field set to None is left out of the JSON. The metadata Anvil provides is in anvil.lib.jsonmodel: bounds (InRange, NonNegative, Chance, Length), JSON shapes (MinMax, Wrapped, Keyed, Hex, Trigger...) and more. GravityWell.__schema__() returns the JSON Schema of the component, and GravityWell.__from_json__(data) builds one back from its parsed JSON.

docs.title: 2. Implementing Logic in TypeScript
docs.text: It is recommended to split your logic into separate files for each block or item, and then register them in your main entry file.

docs.title: Block Logic Example (blocks/myBlock.ts)
docs.text:
import { BlockCustomComponent, StartupEvent } from "@minecraft/server";

const myBlockLogic: BlockCustomComponent = {
    onPlace(e) {
        // Logic when block is placed
    },
    onPlayerInteract(e) {
        // Logic when player interacts with block
    },
};

export function registerMyBlock(startup: StartupEvent) {
    // Note: Use the same identifier as defined in Python
    // Assuming NAMESPACE is imported from your constants file
    startup.blockComponentRegistry.registerCustomComponent(`${NAMESPACE}:my_block_logic`, myBlockLogic);
}

docs.title: Item Logic Example (items/myItem.ts)
docs.text:
import { ItemCustomComponent, StartupEvent } from "@minecraft/server";

const myItemLogic: ItemCustomComponent = {
    onBeforeDurabilityDamage(e) {
        // Logic before durability damage
    },
};

export function registerMyItem(startup: StartupEvent) {
    startup.itemComponentRegistry.registerCustomComponent(`${NAMESPACE}:my_item_logic`, myItemLogic);
}

docs.title: Registering in Main (main.ts)
docs.text:
In your main entry file, listen to the startup event and call your registration functions.

import { system } from "@minecraft/server";
import { registerMyBlock } from "./blocks/myBlock";
import { registerMyItem } from "./items/myItem";

system.beforeEvents.startup.subscribe((startup) => {
    registerMyBlock(startup);
    registerMyItem(startup);
});

docs.title: 3. Reading Parameters in TypeScript
docs.text:
The fields of the Python component arrive as customComponentParameters.params. Define an interface for them and cast.

import { BlockComponentStepOnEvent, CustomComponentParameters } from "@minecraft/server";

interface GravityWellParams {
    pull: number;
    delay: { min: number; max: number };
    color?: string;
}

const gravityWell: BlockCustomComponent = {
    onStepOn(e: BlockComponentStepOnEvent, params: CustomComponentParameters) {
        const { pull, delay } = params.params as GravityWellParams;
        console.log(`Pull ${pull} after ${delay.min}-${delay.max}s`);
    },
};

Ensure your scriptapi flag is enabled when creating your project or added to your anvilconfig.json.

A worked block example with a parameter and states is in Block states, permutations and traits.

docs.title: NPC Dialogues
docs.text:
This tutorial creates a Tinker NPC with a two-scene dialogue: a greeting and a trade screen. Dialogues are behaviour-pack files opened on an NPC entity with the /dialogue command; every string becomes a localization key.

Every snippet compiles as written.

docs.title: The Dialogue
docs.text:
npc/tinker.py
from anvil.api.world.dialogue import Dialogue


def tinker_dialogue():
    dialogue = Dialogue("tinker")

    welcome = dialogue.add_scene("welcome")
    welcome.properties("Tinker", "Need a lantern? I trade brass for ember dust.")
    welcome.button("Trade", ["/dialogue open @s @initiator tut:tinker_trade"])
    welcome.button("Not now", ["/dialogue close @initiator"])
    welcome.set_on_open_commands(["/playsound note.chime @initiator"])

    trade = dialogue.add_scene("tinker_trade")
    trade.properties("Tinker", "Four ember dust for one brass lantern.")
    trade.button(
        "Deal",
        [
            "/clear @initiator tut:ember_dust 0 4",
            "/give @initiator tut:brass_lantern",
            "/dialogue open @s @initiator tut:welcome",
        ],
    )
    trade.button("Back", ["/dialogue open @s @initiator tut:welcome"])
    return dialogue.queue()

The scene tags get the project namespace, so commands refer to them as tut:welcome. The exported scene:

{
  "scene_tag": "tut:welcome",
  "npc_name": {"rawtext": [{"translate": "dialogue.tut:tutorial.npc_name.tinker"}]},
  "text": {"rawtext": [{"translate": "dialogue.tut:tutorial.text.need_a_lantern_i_trade_brass_for_ember_dust"}]},
  "on_open_commands": ["/playsound note.chime @initiator"],
  "buttons": [
    {"name": {"rawtext": [{"translate": "dialogue.tut:tutorial.button.trade"}]}, "commands": ["/dialogue open @s @initiator tut:tinker_trade"]},
    {"name": {"rawtext": [{"translate": "dialogue.tut:tutorial.button.not_now"}]}, "commands": ["/dialogue close @initiator"]}
  ]
}
  • scene.properties(npc_name, text) sets the title and the body.
  • scene.button(name, commands) adds up to six buttons.
  • set_on_open_commands and set_on_close_commands run when the scene is shown or dismissed.

Tip

@initiator is the player who opened the dialogue and @s the NPC. Keep the scene names unique across the whole pack.

docs.title: The NPC
docs.text:
An entity shows dialogues when it has the EntityNPC component. Everything else is a normal entity.

npc entity
from anvil.api.actors.components import (
    EntityAILookAtPlayer,
    EntityCollisionBox,
    EntityHealth,
    EntityKnockbackResistance,
    EntityNPC,
    EntityPersistent,
    EntityPhysics,
    EntityTypeFamily,
)
from anvil.api.actors.entity import Entity
from anvil.api.pbr.texture_set import TextureComponents


def tinker():
    entity = Entity("tinker")
    client = entity.client.description
    client.add_geometry("tinker")
    client.add_texture("tinker", TextureComponents(color="tinker"))
    client.render_controller("default").set_geometry("tinker").add_texture("tinker")

    entity.server.components.add(
        EntityCollisionBox(width=0.6, height=1.9),
        EntityPhysics(has_collision=True, has_gravity=True),
        EntityHealth(value=20, max=20),
        EntityKnockbackResistance(value=1),
        EntityTypeFamily(family=["npc", "tinker"]),
        EntityPersistent(),
        EntityNPC().set_npc_data(skin_list=[0]),
        EntityAILookAtPlayer(priority=1, look_distance=8),
    )
    entity.server.description.config(is_spawnable=False)
    entity.server.event("minecraft:entity_spawned").add_queue_command(
        ["dialogue change @s tut:welcome"]
    )

    tinker_dialogue()
    entity.queue("npc")
    return entity


Tinker = tinker()

Note

EntityNPC needs its npc_data; set_npc_data(skin_list=[0]) is the minimum. The spawn event binds the default scene with dialogue change, so right-clicking the NPC opens it without a command block.

Trading instead of talking

For a villager-style trade screen use a trade table with EntityEconomyTradeTable rather than a dialogue.

docs.title: Animating an Entity
docs.text:
This tutorial builds a Clockwork Golem that idles, walks, attacks and rusts over time. It covers the four moving parts of an animated entity in Anvil: animations from Blockbench, client animation controllers, render controller arrays, and server-side animations and controllers that run commands. Read Adding a Custom Entity first.

The whole example compiles as written. Every name passed to client.animation(...) must exist in assets/bbmodels/clockwork_golem.bbmodel.

docs.title: Register Animations From Blockbench
docs.text:
entities/clockwork_golem.py
from anvil.api.actors.entity import Entity
from anvil.api.pbr.texture_set import TextureComponents

entity = Entity("clockwork_golem")
client = entity.client.description
server = entity.server

client.add_geometry("clockwork_golem")
client.add_texture("clockwork_golem", TextureComponents(color="clockwork_golem"))
client.add_texture("clockwork_golem", TextureComponents(color="clockwork_golem_rusted"))

client.animation("clockwork_golem", "idle")
client.animation("clockwork_golem", "walk")
client.animation("clockwork_golem", "attack")

client.animation(blockbench, animation_name) exports the animation from the Blockbench file and registers it on the client entity under its short name. Pass animate=True to play it unconditionally, or condition= with a Molang expression to play it while the expression is true. Animations driven by a controller need neither.

Two textures, one file

Both textures live in the same .bbmodel. Each client.texture call registers one of them under the name it has in Blockbench.

docs.title: Client Animation Controller
docs.text:
A controller is a state machine. Each state plays animations and lists the transitions out of it, checked in order.

movement controller
from anvil.api.logic.molang import Query

controller = client.animation_controller("movement", animate=True)
controller.add_state("default").animation("idle").transition(
    "walking", Query.GroundSpeed() > 0.1
).transition("attacking", Query.IsDelayedAttacking())
controller.add_state("walking").animation("walk").transition(
    "default", Query.GroundSpeed() < 0.1
).transition("attacking", Query.IsDelayedAttacking()).set_blend_transition(0.2)
controller.add_state("attacking").animation("attack").transition(
    "default", Query.AllAnimationsFinished()
).sound_effect("gear_clank")

client.sound_effect("gear_clank").add_sound("golem/hurt", pitch=0.7)

This exports to animation_controllers/<group>/clockwork_golem.rp_ac.json:

"controller.animation.tut.clockwork_golem.movement": {
  "initial_state": "default",
  "states": {
    "default": {
      "animations": ["idle"],
      "transitions": [{"walking": "(q.ground_speed > 0.1)"}, {"attacking": "q.is_delayed_attacking"}]
    },
    "walking": {
      "animations": ["walk"],
      "transitions": [{"default": "(q.ground_speed < 0.1)"}, {"attacking": "q.is_delayed_attacking"}],
      "blend_transition": 0.2
    },
    "attacking": {
      "animations": ["attack"],
      "transitions": [{"default": "q.all_animations_finished"}],
      "sound_effects": [{"effect": "gear_clank", "locator": "root"}]
    }
  }
}

Molang in Python

Query.GroundSpeed() > 0.1 builds the string (q.ground_speed > 0.1). Comparison, &, | and ~ (not) all work on Query, Variable and Math expressions, so conditions stay readable and typo-free.

Sounds and particles in states

state.sound_effect(name) and state.particle(effect, locator) play when the state is entered. client.sound_effect(name) registers the short name on the entity and returns its sound definition, so you can add the .ogg files from assets/sounds in the same line. See Particles and sounds.

docs.title: Render Controller Arrays
docs.text:
The render controller chooses geometry, textures and materials at render time. Arrays let a Molang expression pick an entry.

render controller
rc = client.render_controller("default")
rc.set_geometry("clockwork_golem")
rc.texture_array(
    "skins", ["clockwork_golem", "clockwork_golem_rusted"], Query.Variant()
)
rc.add_part_visibility("crown", Query.Variant() == 1)
rc.set_is_hurt_color(0.5, 1, 0.2, 0.2)

"controller.render.tut.clockwork_golem.default": {
  "arrays": {"textures": {"array.skins": ["Texture.clockwork_golem", "Texture.clockwork_golem_rusted"]}},
  "geometry": "Geometry.clockwork_golem",
  "textures": ["array.skins[q.variant]"],
  "part_visibility": [{"crown": "(q.variant == 1)"}],
  "is_hurt_color": {"r": 1, "g": 0.2, "b": 0.2, "a": 0.5},
  "materials": [{"*": "material.default"}]
}

Note

add_part_visibility(bone, condition) toggles a bone of the model. geometry_array and material_array work like texture_array. set_on_fire_color, set_overlay_color, set_ignore_lighting() and set_uv_anim(...) are the other common tweaks.

docs.title: Server Components for the Behaviour
docs.text:
The golem fights monsters, so the attack animation has something to react to. EntityAIDelayedAttack is what makes Query.IsDelayedAttacking() true.

server components
from anvil.api.actors.components import (
    EntityAIDelayedAttack,
    EntityAIHurtByTarget,
    EntityAILookAtPlayer,
    EntityAINearestAttackableTarget,
    EntityAIRandomStroll,
    EntityAttack,
    EntityCollisionBox,
    EntityHealth,
    EntityJumpStatic,
    EntityMovement,
    EntityMovementBasic,
    EntityNavigationWalk,
    EntityPhysics,
    EntityVariant,
)
from anvil.api.actors.components.ai_goals import GoalEntityType
from anvil.api.core.filters import Filter

server.components.add(
    EntityCollisionBox(width=1.0, height=1.8),
    EntityPhysics(has_collision=True, has_gravity=True),
    EntityHealth(value=40, max=40),
    EntityMovement(value=0.2),
    EntityMovementBasic(),
    EntityNavigationWalk(can_path_over_water=True),
    EntityJumpStatic(),
    EntityAttack(damage=5),
    EntityAIDelayedAttack(priority=2, attack_duration=0.75, hit_delay_pct=0.5),
    EntityAIHurtByTarget(priority=1),
    EntityAINearestAttackableTarget(
        priority=3,
        must_see=True,
        entity_types=[GoalEntityType(filters=Filter.is_family("monster"), max_dist=16)],
    ),
    EntityAIRandomStroll(priority=5),
    EntityAILookAtPlayer(priority=6),
)

server.component_group("rusted").add(EntityVariant(value=1))
server.event("rust").add_component_groups(["rusted"])

Nested parts

Components with lists of structured entries take small objects, such as GoalEntityType, or have an add_ builder for them (EntityDamageSensor().add_trigger(...)). Filters come from anvil.api.core.filters.Filter; combine them with Filter.all_of([...]) and Filter.any_of([...]).

docs.title: Server Animations and Controllers
docs.text:
Behaviour-pack animations run commands on a timeline. Behaviour-pack controllers run commands when a state is entered or left.

server animations
wind_down = server.description.animation("wind_down", loop=False)
wind_down.set_animation_length(3)
wind_down.add_timeline(0, ["playsound random.click @a[r=8]"])
wind_down.add_timeline(2.5, ["event entity @s rust"])

guard = server.description.animation_controller("guard", animate=True)
guard.add_state("default").transition("alert", Query.HasTarget())
guard.add_state("alert").add_on_entry("playsound note.bell @a[r=16]").transition(
    "default", ~Query.HasTarget()
)

entity.queue("golems")

"animation.tut.clockwork_golem.wind_down": {
  "loop": false,
  "animation_length": 3,
  "timeline": {"0": ["/playsound random.click @a[r=8]"], "2.5": ["/event entity @s rust"]}
}

Playing a server animation

server.description.animation(name, animate=True) plays it from spawn. With animate=False (the default) it is only registered, and a controller state or an event can start it: add state.animation("wind_down") to a behaviour-pack controller state.

docs.title: Full Example — Clockwork Golem
docs.text:
entities/clockwork_golem.py
from anvil.api.actors.components import (
    EntityAIDelayedAttack,
    EntityAIHurtByTarget,
    EntityAILookAtPlayer,
    EntityAINearestAttackableTarget,
    EntityAIRandomStroll,
    EntityAttack,
    EntityCollisionBox,
    EntityHealth,
    EntityJumpStatic,
    EntityMovement,
    EntityMovementBasic,
    EntityNavigationWalk,
    EntityPhysics,
    EntityVariant,
)
from anvil.api.actors.components.ai_goals import GoalEntityType
from anvil.api.actors.entity import Entity
from anvil.api.core.filters import Filter
from anvil.api.logic.molang import Query
from anvil.api.pbr.texture_set import TextureComponents


def clockwork_golem():
    entity = Entity("clockwork_golem")
    client = entity.client.description
    server = entity.server

    client.add_geometry("clockwork_golem")
    client.add_texture("clockwork_golem", TextureComponents(color="clockwork_golem"))
    client.add_texture("clockwork_golem", TextureComponents(color="clockwork_golem_rusted"))

    client.animation("clockwork_golem", "idle")
    client.animation("clockwork_golem", "walk")
    client.animation("clockwork_golem", "attack")

    controller = client.animation_controller("movement", animate=True)
    controller.add_state("default").animation("idle").transition(
        "walking", Query.GroundSpeed() > 0.1
    ).transition("attacking", Query.IsDelayedAttacking())
    controller.add_state("walking").animation("walk").transition(
        "default", Query.GroundSpeed() < 0.1
    ).transition("attacking", Query.IsDelayedAttacking()).set_blend_transition(0.2)
    controller.add_state("attacking").animation("attack").transition(
        "default", Query.AllAnimationsFinished()
    ).sound_effect("gear_clank")

    client.sound_effect("gear_clank").add_sound("golem/hurt", pitch=0.7)

    rc = client.render_controller("default")
    rc.set_geometry("clockwork_golem")
    rc.texture_array(
        "skins", ["clockwork_golem", "clockwork_golem_rusted"], Query.Variant()
    )
    rc.add_part_visibility("crown", Query.Variant() == 1)
    rc.set_is_hurt_color(0.5, 1, 0.2, 0.2)

    server.components.add(
        EntityCollisionBox(width=1.0, height=1.8),
        EntityPhysics(has_collision=True, has_gravity=True),
        EntityHealth(value=40, max=40),
        EntityMovement(value=0.2),
        EntityMovementBasic(),
        EntityNavigationWalk(can_path_over_water=True),
        EntityJumpStatic(),
        EntityAttack(damage=5),
        EntityAIDelayedAttack(priority=2, attack_duration=0.75, hit_delay_pct=0.5),
        EntityAIHurtByTarget(priority=1),
        EntityAINearestAttackableTarget(
            priority=3,
            must_see=True,
            entity_types=[GoalEntityType(filters=Filter.is_family("monster"), max_dist=16)],
        ),
        EntityAIRandomStroll(priority=5),
        EntityAILookAtPlayer(priority=6),
    )

    server.component_group("rusted").add(EntityVariant(value=1))
    server.event("rust").add_component_groups(["rusted"])

    wind_down = server.description.animation("wind_down", loop=False)
    wind_down.set_animation_length(3)
    wind_down.add_timeline(0, ["playsound random.click @a[r=8]"])
    wind_down.add_timeline(2.5, ["event entity @s rust"])

    guard = server.description.animation_controller("guard", animate=True)
    guard.add_state("default").transition("alert", Query.HasTarget())
    guard.add_state("alert").add_on_entry("playsound note.bell @a[r=16]").transition(
        "default", ~Query.HasTarget()
    )

    entity.queue("golems")
    return entity


ClockworkGolem = clockwork_golem()

docs.title: Localization in Anvil
docs.text: This page explains how Anvil handles localization keys and the localization CSV, and how to translate/export languages correctly.

docs.title: How keys are created
docs.text:
Whenever you pass a plain string to an Anvil component, Anvil automatically:

  1. Creates a localization key for that string, and
