  2. Writes the key–value pair into the CSV file at your project root (e.g., localization.csv).
examples that create keys
ItemDisplayName("Arcane User Guide")
BlockDisplayName("Enchanting Plus Table")
# Any other component argument that is a plain string will be tracked too

Where it goes

The English source string is saved under the en_US column as the value for the generated key. The same key is also created in the other Minecraft-supported locale columns inside the same CSV, with empty values until you translate them.

docs.title: Translating other languages
docs.text:
You have two options for non‑English locales:

  • Manual translation: open localization.csv and fill in the empty values in the non-en_US language columns.
  • Automatic translation: call anvil.translate() to auto-fill missing values using Google Translate.
auto translate missing locales
# Populates only empty cells in non-en_US language columns via Google Translate
import anvil
anvil.translate()

Note

anvil.translate() does not overwrite values that are already translated — whether they were filled manually or by a previous run. It only fills empty cells.

docs.title: What happens when strings change
docs.text:
• If you change the source text in code, the corresponding key's value is updated in en_US and the old value is removed from the other language columns.
  • If you delete a plain string from your Anvil code, its entry is removed from the CSV.

Warning

Keep your source of truth in code: adding text directly in localization.csv that does not exist in code will not be referenced at build time.

docs.title: Build vs package behavior
docs.text:
• anvil compile() → compiles only en_us.
  • anvil.package(), anvil.mcaddon(), anvil.mcworld() → compile all languages present in localization.csv.

Tip

Any language column that has a key with an empty value will not be exported to the final .lang file. Make sure you fill required translations before packaging.

docs.title: Quick checklist
docs.text:
• Use plain strings in components; Anvil will create keys automatically.
  • Verify keys and values in localization.csv -> en_US is the source of truth.
  • Translate others manually or with anvil.translate().
  • Remember build rules: compile = English only, packaging commands = all languages.
  • Empty values in a locale column -> that locale won't export to .lang.

docs.title: Particles and Sounds
docs.text:
This tutorial adds a particle burst and sounds to the Ember Moth from Spawn rules and loot: a particle from assets/particles, sound definitions from assets/sounds, entity sound events, and block sounds.

Every snippet compiles as written.

docs.title: Particles
docs.text:
Particles are JSON files you author in a particle editor and drop in assets/particles/<name>.particle.json, next to their texture <name>.png. Anvil reads the file into its typed particle format, checks that the identifier inside matches the file name, and exports the file and the texture. A key or component the format does not have stops the build with the file and key named. Particle.__schema__() returns the JSON Schema of the format, which an editor can use to check particle files.

particle
from anvil.api.pbr.texture_set import TextureComponents
from anvil.api.world.particles import Particle

Particle("ember_burst", TextureComponents(color="ember_burst")).queue()

A particle can then be referenced from an entity, an animation controller state or a /particle command as <namespace>:ember_burst.

particle on the entity
from anvil.api.logic.molang import Query

client = entity.client.description
client.particle_effect("ember_burst", TextureComponents(color="ember_burst"))
sparks = client.animation_controller("sparks", animate=True)
sparks.add_state("default").transition("hurt", Query.HurtTime() > 0)
sparks.add_state("hurt").particle("ember_burst", locator="root").transition(
    "default", ~(Query.HurtTime() > 0)
)

"controller.animation.tut.ember_moth.sparks": {
  "initial_state": "default",
  "states": {
    "default": {"transitions": [{"hurt": "(q.hurt_time > 0)"}]},
    "hurt": {
      "transitions": [{"default": "!((q.hurt_time > 0))"}],
      "particle_effects": [{"effect": "ember_burst", "locator": "root"}]
    }
  }
}

PBR particles

TextureComponents(color="ember_burst", mer="ember_burst_mer") exports a texture set for the particle when PBR is enabled.

docs.title: Sound Definitions
docs.text:
A sound definition is a named list of .ogg files from assets/sounds. The name gets the project namespace.

sound definitions
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel.enums import SoundCategory
from anvil.api.sounds.sound_definitions import SoundDefinition


def ember_moth_sounds():
    sounds = SoundDefinition()
    flutter = sounds.sound_reference("mob.ember_moth.flutter", SoundCategory.Neutral)
    flutter.add_sound("golem/idle_0", volume=0.6, pitch=1.4)
    flutter.add_sound("golem/idle_1", volume=0.6, pitch=1.6)
    sounds.sound_reference("mob.ember_moth.hurt", SoundCategory.Neutral).add_sound(
        "golem/hurt"
    )
    sounds.sound_reference("mob.ember_moth.death", SoundCategory.Neutral).add_sound(
        "golem/death"
    )
    sounds.queue()

"tut:mob.ember_moth.flutter": {
  "category": "neutral",
  "sounds": [
    {"name": "sounds/tut/golem/idle_0", "volume": 0.6, "pitch": 1.4},
    {"name": "sounds/tut/golem/idle_1", "volume": 0.6, "pitch": 1.6}
  ]
}

Note

add_sound("golem/idle_0") reads assets/sounds/golem/idle_0.ogg. Several sounds under one reference are picked at random, weighted by weight. SoundDefinition() is a single shared file, so call it from anywhere.

docs.title: Entity Sound Events
docs.text:
Sound events connect the game's events (ambient, hurt, death, step...) to a sound definition.

sound events
from anvil.api.actors.components import EntityAmbientSoundInterval
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel.enums import EntitySoundEvent

client.sound_event("mob.ember_moth.flutter", EntitySoundEvent.Ambient, volume=0.8)
client.sound_event("mob.ember_moth.hurt", EntitySoundEvent.Hurt)
client.sound_event("mob.ember_moth.death", EntitySoundEvent.Death)

server.components.add(
    EntityAmbientSoundInterval(value=4, range=8, event_name="ambient"),
)

"tut:ember_moth": {
  "events": {
    "ambient": {"sound": "tut:mob.ember_moth.flutter", "pitch": [0.8, 1.2], "volume": 0.8},
    "hurt": {"sound": "tut:mob.ember_moth.hurt", "pitch": [0.8, 1.2], "volume": 1.0},
    "death": {"sound": "tut:mob.ember_moth.death", "pitch": [0.8, 1.2], "volume": 1.0}
  }
}

Note

The ambient event only plays when the server component EntityAmbientSoundInterval is present; value is the seconds between sounds and range the random extra.

Sounds from controllers

For a sound played by an animation controller state use client.sound_effect(name), which registers the short name on the entity and returns its sound definition. See Animating an entity.

docs.title: Block Sounds
docs.text:
block sounds
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel.enums import BlockSoundEvent, BlockSoundGroup

block.client.sound_group(BlockSoundGroup.Chain)
block.client.block_sound("block.brass_lantern.hit", BlockSoundEvent.Hit).add_sound(
    "golem/hurt"
)

A sound group reuses a vanilla block's sounds. block_sound(reference, event) maps one of the block's events to your own definition and returns it, so the files are added in place.

docs.title: Music
docs.text:
music
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel.enums import MusicCategory
from anvil.api.sounds.music_definitions import MusicDefinition

music = MusicDefinition()
music.music_definition(MusicCategory.Creative, min_delay=30, max_delay=120).add_sound(
    "music/ember_theme", stream=True
)
music.queue()

A biome plays its own music through biome.client.biome_music(music_definition=...), see Creating a biome.

docs.title: Full Example — Ember Moth
docs.text:
entities/ember_moth.py
from anvil.api.actors.components import (
    EntityAIRandomHover,
    EntityAmbientSoundInterval,
    EntityCollisionBox,
    EntityDespawn,
    EntityFireImmune,
    EntityFlyingSpeed,
    EntityHealth,
    EntityLoot,
    EntityMovementBasic,
    EntityNavigationFly,
    EntityPhysics,
    EntityTypeFamily,
)
from anvil.api.actors.entity import Entity
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel.enums import (
    Difficulty,
    EntitySoundEvent,
    Population,
    SoundCategory,
)
from anvil.api.core.filters import Filter
from anvil.api.logic.molang import Query
from anvil.api.pbr.texture_set import TextureComponents
from anvil.api.sounds.sound_definitions import SoundDefinition
from anvil.api.vanilla.biomes import MinecraftBiomeTags
from anvil.api.vanilla.blocks import MinecraftBlockTypes
from anvil.api.vanilla.items import MinecraftItemTypes
from anvil.api.world.loot_tables import LootTable
from anvil.api.world.particles import Particle


def ember_moth_loot():
    table = LootTable("ember_moth")
    pool = table.pool(rolls=1)
    pool.entry("tut:ember_dust", count=1, weight=4)
    pool.entry(MinecraftItemTypes.Gunpowder(), count=1, weight=1)
    pool.entry(None, weight=2)

    rare = table.pool(rolls=1)
    rare.conditions.killed_by_player().random_chance_with_looting(0.05, 0.02)
    rare.entry(MinecraftItemTypes.BlazePowder(), count=1)
    table.queue()
    return table


def ember_moth_sounds():
    sounds = SoundDefinition()
    flutter = sounds.sound_reference("mob.ember_moth.flutter", SoundCategory.Neutral)
    flutter.add_sound("golem/idle_0", volume=0.6, pitch=1.4)
    flutter.add_sound("golem/idle_1", volume=0.6, pitch=1.6)
    sounds.sound_reference("mob.ember_moth.hurt", SoundCategory.Neutral).add_sound(
        "golem/hurt"
    )
    sounds.sound_reference("mob.ember_moth.death", SoundCategory.Neutral).add_sound(
        "golem/death"
    )
    sounds.queue()


def ember_moth():
    entity = Entity("ember_moth")
    client = entity.client.description
    server = entity.server

    client.add_geometry("ember_moth")
    client.add_texture("ember_moth", TextureComponents(color="ember_moth"))
    client.animation("ember_moth", "fly", animate=True)
    rc = client.render_controller("default")
    rc.set_geometry("ember_moth")
    rc.add_texture("ember_moth")
    rc.set_ignore_lighting()

    Particle("ember_burst", TextureComponents(color="ember_burst")).queue()
    client.particle_effect("ember_burst", TextureComponents(color="ember_burst"))
    sparks = client.animation_controller("sparks", animate=True)
    sparks.add_state("default").transition("hurt", Query.HurtTime() > 0)
    sparks.add_state("hurt").particle("ember_burst", locator="root").transition(
        "default", ~(Query.HurtTime() > 0)
    )

    client.sound_event("mob.ember_moth.flutter", EntitySoundEvent.Ambient, volume=0.8)
    client.sound_event("mob.ember_moth.hurt", EntitySoundEvent.Hurt)
    client.sound_event("mob.ember_moth.death", EntitySoundEvent.Death)

    server.components.add(
        EntityCollisionBox(width=0.5, height=0.4),
        EntityPhysics(has_collision=True, has_gravity=False),
        EntityHealth(value=6, max=6),
        EntityTypeFamily(family=["ember_moth", "ambient", "mob"]),
        EntityFireImmune(),
        EntityFlyingSpeed(value=0.15),
        EntityMovementBasic(),
        EntityNavigationFly(can_path_from_air=True),
        EntityAIRandomHover(priority=1, hover_height=(2, 6), xz_dist=8, y_dist=6),
        EntityAmbientSoundInterval(value=4, range=8, event_name="ambient"),
        EntityDespawn(despawn_from_distance=(32, 64)),
        EntityLoot(table=ember_moth_loot()),
    )

    spawn = server.spawn_rule
    spawn.description.set_population_control(Population.Ambient)
    spawn.add_condition.spawns_on_surface().brightness_filter(0, 7).weight(8).herd(
        2, 5
    ).biome_filter(
        [
            Filter.any_of(
                [
                    Filter.has_biome_tag(MinecraftBiomeTags.Savanna),
                    Filter.has_biome_tag(MinecraftBiomeTags.Mesa),
                ]
            )
        ]
    ).spawns_above_block_filter([MinecraftBlockTypes.Magma()], distance=4)
    spawn.add_condition.spawns_underground().difficulty_filter(
        Difficulty.Easy, Difficulty.Hard
    ).weight(2).biome_filter([Filter.has_biome_tag(MinecraftBiomeTags.Nether)])

    ember_moth_sounds()
    entity.set_display_name("Ember Moth", "Ember Moth Egg").queue("ambient")
    return entity


EmberMoth = ember_moth()

docs.title: Assets & Textures
docs.text: This guide explains how to manage Textures, Animations, and PBR (Physically Based Rendering) in Anvil.

docs.title: Block & Entity Assets
docs.text: For Blocks and Entities, textures and animations are not stored as separate image files in your resource pack. Instead, they must be embedded inside the Blockbench model file (.bbmodel).

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Create your model in Blockbench.
  2. Import your textures (Color, Normal, MER) into the Blockbench project.
  3. Save the model as a .bbmodel file.
  4. Place the file in assets/bbmodels/ (e.g., assets/bbmodels/my_model.bbmodel).

Anvil will automatically extract the textures, processing PBR maps like Normal and MER (Metalness/Emissive/Roughness) during the build.

docs.title: PBR Blocks Example
docs.text:
Here is a production-ready example demonstrating a Mystic Crystal block. It uses:

  • PBR Textures: Color, MER, and Height maps.
  • Render Method: Blending for transparency/translucency.
blocks/mystic_crystal.py
from anvil.api.blocks.blocks import Block
from anvil.api.blocks.components import (
    BlockGeometry,
    BlockMaterialInstance,
    InstanceSpec,
    InstanceVariant,
    MaterialParams,
)
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel.enums import BlockFaceValues, BlockMaterial

block = Block("mystic_crystal")
block.server.components.add(
    BlockGeometry(blockbench="mystic_crystal"),
    BlockMaterialInstance().add_instance(
        spec=InstanceSpec(
            blockbench="mystic_crystal",
            face=BlockFaceValues.All,
            variations=[
                InstanceVariant(
                    # These texture names must match what is inside 'mystic_crystal.bbmodel'
                    color="mystic_crystal_texture",
                    mer="mystic_crystal_mer",
                    height="mystic_crystal_height",
                )
            ],
            params=MaterialParams(render_method=BlockMaterial.Blend),
        )
    ),
)
block.queue()

A flipbook animates the texture: give InstanceSpec several InstanceVariants (one per frame, all in the same Blockbench file) and flipbooks=[FlipbookParams(frames=[0, 1, 2, 3], ticks_per_frame=20)].

Do not use loose PNGs

Do not place block or entity textures in assets/textures/. They will be ignored. Usage of the Blockbench file is mandatory for these assets.

docs.title: PBR Entities Example
docs.text:
This example shows a Mystic Wisp entity using PBR textures defined in its client description.

entities/mystic_wisp.py
from anvil.api.actors.entity import Entity
from anvil.api.pbr.texture_set import TextureComponents

def mystic_wisp():
    entity = Entity("mystic_wisp")

    # Define the geometry and textures (must be in 'mystic_wisp.bbmodel')
    entity.client.description.add_geometry("mystic_wisp")
    entity.client.description.add_texture(
        blockbench="mystic_wisp",
        component=TextureComponents(
            color="mystic_wisp",
            mer="mystic_wisp_mer",
            height="mystic_wisp_height"
        ),
    )

    # Render Controller
    rc = entity.client.description.render_controller("default")
    rc.set_geometry("mystic_wisp")
    rc.add_texture("mystic_wisp")

    return entity.queue()

docs.title: PBR Textures
docs.text:
Anvil supports Minecraft's PBR system. If you include PBR maps in your Blockbench model, they are automatically handled.

Map Type Conventional Key Description Color name Base color texture. Normal name_normal Surface bumpiness/depth. MER name_mer Metalness (Red), Emissive (Green), Roughness (Blue). Height name_height Displacement (exclusive with Normal).

docs.title: Item Assets
docs.text:
Unlike Blocks and Entities, Items typically use standalone texture files.

  • Location: Place your .png files in assets/textures/items/.
  • Naming: The filename (without extension) is referenced in your code.
from anvil.api.items.components import ItemIcon
from anvil.api.pbr.texture_set import TextureComponents

# References 'assets/textures/items/my_item.png'
ItemIcon(textures=TextureComponents(color="my_item"))

docs.title: World Settings
docs.text: Vibrant Visuals also has world-level files: LightingSettings, AtmosphericSettings, FogSettings, WaterSettings, ColorGradingSettings, ShadowSettings and LocalLighting in anvil.api.pbr. Creating a biome builds a full set and attaches it to a biome.

docs.title: Recipes and the Item Catalog
docs.text:
This tutorial defines two materials, Ember Dust and Ember Crystal, and every recipe type Anvil exports: shapeless, shaped, smelting and stonecutter, then groups the items in the creative inventory with the crafting item catalog.

Every snippet compiles as written.

docs.title: The Items
docs.text:
recipes/ember_recipes.py
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel.enums import ItemCategory
from anvil.api.items.components import ItemDisplayName, ItemIcon, ItemMaxStackSize
from anvil.api.items.items import Item
from anvil.api.pbr.texture_set import TextureComponents


def simple_item(name: str, display: str) -> Item:
    item = Item(name)
    item.server.description.set_menu_category(ItemCategory.Items)
    item.server.components.add(
        ItemIcon(textures=TextureComponents(color=name)),
        ItemDisplayName(value=display),
        ItemMaxStackSize(value=64),
    )
    return item.queue()


dust = simple_item("ember_dust", "Ember Dust")
crystal = simple_item("ember_crystal", "Ember Crystal")

Tip

queue() returns the object, so a helper can create, queue and return an item in one expression. Items, blocks, vanilla MinecraftItemTypes.X() and MinecraftBlockTypes.X() descriptors and plain "namespace:name" strings are all accepted wherever a recipe wants an item.

docs.title: Shapeless
docs.text:
shapeless
from anvil.api.items.crafting.shapeless import ShapelessRecipe
from anvil.api.vanilla.items import MinecraftItemTypes

ShapelessRecipe("ember_dust").ingredients(
    [MinecraftItemTypes.BlazePowder(), (MinecraftItemTypes.Gunpowder(), 2)]
).result(dust, count=3).unlock_items([MinecraftItemTypes.BlazePowder()]).queue()

An (item, count) tuple asks for several of one ingredient. unlock_items lists the items that reveal the recipe in the recipe book; unlock_context(RecipeUnlockContext.AlwaysUnlocked) is the alternative.

docs.title: Shaped
docs.text:
shaped
from anvil.api.items.crafting.shaped import ShapedCraftingRecipe

ShapedCraftingRecipe("ember_crystal").ingredients(
    [
        [None, dust, None],
        [dust, MinecraftItemTypes.AmethystShard(), dust],
        [None, dust, None],
    ]
).result(crystal).unlock_items([dust]).queue()

"minecraft:recipe_shaped": {
  "description": {"identifier": "tut:ember_crystal"},
  "tags": ["crafting_table"],
  "unlock": [{"item": "tut:ember_dust"}],
  "assume_symmetry": true,
  "pattern": [" a ", "aba", " a "],
  "key": {"a": {"item": "tut:ember_dust"}, "b": {"item": "minecraft:amethyst_shard"}},
  "result": {"item": "tut:ember_crystal", "count": 1}
}

The grid is a list of rows; None is an empty slot. Anvil assigns the pattern keys. Pass assume_symmetry=False to the constructor when the mirrored pattern must not match.

docs.title: Smelting and Stonecutting
docs.text:
furnace and stonecutter
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel.enums import SmeltingTags
from anvil.api.items.crafting.furnace import SmeltingRecipe
from anvil.api.items.crafting.shapeless import StoneCutterRecipe
from anvil.api.vanilla.blocks import MinecraftBlockTypes

SmeltingRecipe(
    "ember_dust_from_crystal", [SmeltingTags.FURNACE, SmeltingTags.BLAST_FURNACE]
).input(crystal).output(dust).queue()

StoneCutterRecipe("ember_crystal_from_block").ingredient(
    MinecraftBlockTypes.AmethystBlock()
).result(crystal, count=4).queue()

Note

Smelting recipes list the blocks they work in: FURNACE, BLAST_FURNACE, SMOKER, CAMPFIRE and SOUL_CAMPFIRE. Smithing recipes live in anvil.api.items.crafting.smithing_transform and smithing_trim, brewing in brewing.

docs.title: Crafting Item Catalog
Full Example
docs.text:
recipes/ember_recipes.py
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel.enums import ItemCategory, SmeltingTags
from anvil.api.items.components import ItemDisplayName, ItemIcon, ItemMaxStackSize
from anvil.api.items.crafting.catalog import CraftingItemCatalog
from anvil.api.items.crafting.furnace import SmeltingRecipe
from anvil.api.items.crafting.shaped import ShapedCraftingRecipe
from anvil.api.items.crafting.shapeless import ShapelessRecipe, StoneCutterRecipe
from anvil.api.items.items import Item
from anvil.api.pbr.texture_set import TextureComponents
from anvil.api.vanilla.blocks import MinecraftBlockTypes
from anvil.api.vanilla.items import MinecraftItemTypes


def simple_item(name: str, display: str) -> Item:
    item = Item(name)
    item.server.description.set_menu_category(ItemCategory.Items)
    item.server.components.add(
        ItemIcon(textures=TextureComponents(color=name)),
        ItemDisplayName(value=display),
        ItemMaxStackSize(value=64),
    )
    return item.queue()


def ember_recipes():
    dust = simple_item("ember_dust", "Ember Dust")
    crystal = simple_item("ember_crystal", "Ember Crystal")

    ShapelessRecipe("ember_dust").ingredients(
        [MinecraftItemTypes.BlazePowder(), (MinecraftItemTypes.Gunpowder(), 2)]
    ).result(dust, count=3).unlock_items([MinecraftItemTypes.BlazePowder()]).queue()

    ShapedCraftingRecipe("ember_crystal").ingredients(
        [
            [None, dust, None],
            [dust, MinecraftItemTypes.AmethystShard(), dust],
            [None, dust, None],
        ]
    ).result(crystal).unlock_items([dust]).queue()

    SmeltingRecipe(
        "ember_dust_from_crystal", [SmeltingTags.FURNACE, SmeltingTags.BLAST_FURNACE]
    ).input(crystal).output(dust).queue()

    StoneCutterRecipe("ember_crystal_from_block").ingredient(
        MinecraftBlockTypes.AmethystBlock()
    ).result(crystal, count=4).queue()

    catalog = CraftingItemCatalog()
    catalog.add_group(ItemCategory.Items, "Ember Materials", dust, [dust, crystal])
    catalog.queue()


ember_recipes()

docs.title: Spawn Rules and Loot
docs.text:
This tutorial gives an Ember Moth, a small flying mob, natural spawn rules and a loot table. The moth is also used in Particles and sounds; the full entity is at the end of that page. Read Adding a Custom Entity first.

Every snippet compiles as written.

docs.title: A Flying Mob
docs.text:
entities/ember_moth.py
from anvil.api.actors.components import (
    EntityAIRandomHover,
    EntityCollisionBox,
    EntityDespawn,
    EntityFireImmune,
    EntityFlyingSpeed,
    EntityHealth,
    EntityMovementBasic,
    EntityNavigationFly,
    EntityPhysics,
    EntityTypeFamily,
)
from anvil.api.actors.entity import Entity

entity = Entity("ember_moth")
server = entity.server

server.components.add(
    EntityCollisionBox(width=0.5, height=0.4),
    EntityPhysics(has_collision=True, has_gravity=False),
    EntityHealth(value=6, max=6),
    EntityTypeFamily(family=["ember_moth", "ambient", "mob"]),
    EntityFireImmune(),
    EntityFlyingSpeed(value=0.15),
    EntityMovementBasic(),
    EntityNavigationFly(can_path_from_air=True),
    EntityAIRandomHover(priority=1, hover_height=(2, 6), xz_dist=8, y_dist=6),
    EntityDespawn(despawn_from_distance=(32, 64)),
)

Note

A flyer needs has_gravity=False, a flying speed, a fly navigation and a goal that moves it. EntityDespawn keeps the world from filling up with moths.

docs.title: Loot Table
Spawn Rules
docs.text:
Every entity server has a spawn rule. Each add_condition starts a new condition block; a mob spawns when all parts of a block pass.

spawn rules
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel.enums import Difficulty, Population
from anvil.api.core.filters import Filter
from anvil.api.vanilla.biomes import MinecraftBiomeTags
from anvil.api.vanilla.blocks import MinecraftBlockTypes

spawn = server.spawn_rule
spawn.description.set_population_control(Population.Ambient)
spawn.add_condition.spawns_on_surface().brightness_filter(0, 7).weight(8).herd(
    2, 5
).biome_filter(
    [
        Filter.any_of(
            [
                Filter.has_biome_tag(MinecraftBiomeTags.Savanna),
                Filter.has_biome_tag(MinecraftBiomeTags.Mesa),
            ]
        )
    ]
).spawns_above_block_filter([MinecraftBlockTypes.Magma()], distance=4)
spawn.add_condition.spawns_underground().difficulty_filter(
    Difficulty.Easy, Difficulty.Hard
).weight(2).biome_filter([Filter.has_biome_tag(MinecraftBiomeTags.Nether)])

entity.set_display_name("Ember Moth", "Ember Moth Egg").queue("ambient")

"conditions": [
  {
    "minecraft:spawns_on_surface": {},
    "minecraft:brightness_filter": {"min": 0, "max": 7, "adjust_for_weather": true},
    "minecraft:weight": {"default": 8},
    "minecraft:herd": [{"min_size": 2, "max_size": 5}],
    "minecraft:biome_filter": [{"any_of": [{"test": "has_biome_tag", "value": "savanna"}, {"test": "has_biome_tag", "value": "mesa"}]}],
    "minecraft:spawns_above_block_filter": {"blocks": ["minecraft:magma"], "distance": 4}
  },
  {
    "minecraft:spawns_underground": {},
    "minecraft:difficulty_filter": {"min": "easy", "max": "hard"},
    "minecraft:weight": {"default": 2},
    "minecraft:biome_filter": [{"test": "has_biome_tag", "value": "nether"}]
  }
]

Note

biome_filter takes a list of filters. The other builders are height_filter, distance_filter, density_limit, delay_filter, spawns_on_block_filter, spawns_underwater, spawns_in_lava, permute_type, player_in_village_filter, world_age_filter and spawn_event.

No natural spawning

Skip spawn_rule and call entity.server.description.config(is_spawnable=False) for a mob that only appears through commands or scripts.

docs.title: Creating Trade Tables
docs.text: This guide explains how to define trading options for villagers using the TradeTable API. Trade tables allow you to customize what items entities buy and sell, organize them into unlockable tiers, and group them for randomized selection.

docs.title: Direct API Usage
docs.text:
The TradeTable API uses a fluent interface, allowing you to chain methods to build your hierarchy of tiers, groups, and trades.

trading/my_trader.py
from anvil.api.world.trade_tables import TradeTable
from anvil.api.vanilla.items import MinecraftItemTypes

# 1. Create the table
table = TradeTable("my_trader")

# 2. Add a Tier (Level 1, 0 XP required)
tier_1 = table.tier(total_exp_required=0)

# 3. Add a Group (Selects 1 trade from the list)
group_1 = tier_1.group(num_to_select=1)

# 4. Add a specific Trade
# Wants 1 Emerald -> Gives 5 Apples
group_1.trade(max_uses=7, reward_exp=True).add_wants(
    MinecraftItemTypes.Emerald(), quantity=1
).add_gives(
    MinecraftItemTypes.Apple(), quantity=5
)

# You can also chain everything in one go:
table.tier(total_exp_required=10).group(num_to_select=2).trade(
    max_uses=5
).add_wants(
    MinecraftItemTypes.Diamond(), 1
).add_gives(
    "my_custom:sword", 1
)

# 5. Queue for export
table.queue()

Export rule

You must call .queue() on your TradeTable object. If you skip this, Anvil will not export the JSON file to your behavior pack.

Items

You can use string identifiers (e.g. "minecraft:apple"), Identifier objects, or Anvil's typed helpers (like MinecraftItemTypes.Apple()) for items.

docs.title: Data-Driven Approach
docs.text:
For complex traders with many tiers and options, defining trades in a dictionary and looping through it can be cleaner and more maintainable.

trading/harbour_folk_trades.py
from anvil.api.world.trade_tables import TradeTable
from anvil.api.vanilla.items import MinecraftItemTypes

def create_trades():
    # Define your data structure
    trades_data = {
        "novice": {
            "min_experience": 0,
            "groups": [
                {
                    "select": 1,
                    "trades": [
                        {
                            "wants": [{"item": MinecraftItemTypes.Emerald(), "count": 1}],
                            "gives": [{"item": MinecraftItemTypes.Bread(), "count": 6}],
                            "stock": 16,
                            "xp": 2
                        }
                    ]
                }
            ]
        },
        "apprentice": {
            "min_experience": 10,
            "groups": [
                {
                    "select": 1,
                    "trades": [
                        {
                            "wants": [{"item": MinecraftItemTypes.IronIngot(), "count": 4}],
                            "gives": [{"item": MinecraftItemTypes.Emerald(), "count": 1}],
                            "stock": 12,
                            "xp": 10
                        }
                    ]
                }
            ]
        }
    }

    # Create the table object
    trade_table = TradeTable("harbour_folk_resource_trader")

    # Loop through the data to build the table
    for level, data in trades_data.items():
        # Create the tier
        tier = trade_table.tier(data["min_experience"])

        for group_data in data["groups"]:
            # Create a group within the tier
            trade_group = tier.group(group_data["select"])

            for trade_def in group_data["trades"]:
                # Create the trade
                trade = trade_group.trade(
                    max_uses=trade_def.get("stock", 10),
                    reward_exp=True,
                    trader_exp=trade_def.get("xp", 1),
                )

                # Add 'wants' (Cost)
                for want in trade_def["wants"]:
                    trade.add_wants(
                        item=want["item"],
                        quantity=want["count"],
                        price_multiplier=0.05
                    )

                # Add 'gives' (Reward)
                for give in trade_def["gives"]:
                    trade.add_gives(
                        item=give["item"],
                        quantity=give["count"]
                    )

    # Queue the table for export
    trade_table.queue()
    return trade_table

Structure

The hierarchy is always Table -> Tiers -> Groups -> Trades. - Tiers unlock based on villager XP. - Groups determine how many trades are picked from a pool (useful for RNG). - Trades define the actual exchange (inputs/outputs).

docs.title: Modifying Trades
docs.text:
The .add_gives() method returns the given item, which has the loot table function builders. This allows you to add modifiers like enchantments to the traded item.

# Trade that gives an enchanted sword
trade.add_gives(MinecraftItemTypes.IronSword(), 1).EnchantWithLevels(
    (20, 30), treasure=True
)

docs.title: Attaching the Table to an Entity
docs.text:
from anvil.api.actors.components import EntityAITradeWithPlayer, EntityEconomyTradeTable

entity.server.components.add(
    EntityEconomyTradeTable(table=table, display_name="Tinker"),
    EntityAITradeWithPlayer(priority=1),
)

EntityEconomyTradeTable accepts the TradeTable object or a path string. EntityAITradeWithPlayer is the AI goal that opens the trade screen.

Efficiency

Using the loop approach is recommended for entities with standard profession hierarchies (Novice, Apprentice, Journeyman, etc.) to keep your code DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself).

docs.title: Using Jigsaw Structures
docs.text:
This guide explains how to generate complex, procedural structures using Jigsaw Blocks, similar to Minecraft's villages or bastions. We will stick to the patterns used in complex addon projects.

The system consists of three main parts:

  1. Processors: Rules for how blocks behave during placement (e.g., ignoring air, replacing water).
  2. Template Pools: Collections of structure files (.mcstructure) that can spawn.
  3. Structure Sets: The top-level definition that controls where and how the structures generate in the world.

docs.title: 1. Processors
docs.text:
Processors allow you to modify blocks as they are placed. For example, you might want a path to replace grass but not air.

world/structures.py
from anvil.api.world.structures import _JigsawStructureProcess
from anvil.api.vanilla.blocks import MinecraftBlockTypes

# Create a processor that prevents structure air from overwriting world blocks
# and ensures paths replace dirt correctly.
def create_path_processor():
    processor = _JigsawStructureProcess("ignore_air")

    # Don't replace existing blocks with Structure Void/Air
    processor.add_block_ignore_processor([MinecraftBlockTypes.Air()])

    # Rule: structure dirt is placed as a grass path
    rule = processor.add_block_rule()
    rule.input_predicate.block_state_match(MinecraftBlockTypes.Dirt())
    rule.set_output_state(MinecraftBlockTypes.GrassPath())
    return processor

ignore_air = create_path_processor()

docs.title: 2. Template Pools
docs.text:
Pools are groups of structure elements. You often have a "start" pool and then subsequent pools like "corridors", "rooms", or "loot_rooms".

from anvil.api.world.structures import JigsawStructureTemplatePool

pools = []

def dungeon_start_pool():
    # The name "dungeon_start" corresponds to the pool name referenced in Jigsaw blocks
    # Note: In the jigsaw block, you must use a unique NAMESPACE:POOL_NAME. Anvil will automaticall use the namespace of the addon.
    pool = JigsawStructureTemplatePool("dungeon_start")

    # Add an element pointing to assets/structures/dungeon/start.mcstructure
    # We apply the processor we created earlier
    pool.add_structure_element("dungeon/start", ignore_air)

    pools.append(pool)
    return pool

def rooms_pool():
    pool = JigsawStructureTemplatePool("dungeon_rooms")

    # Add multiple variants with different weights
    pool.add_structure_element("dungeon/room_large", ignore_air, weight=10)
    pool.add_structure_element("dungeon/room_small", ignore_air, weight=5)

    pools.append(pool)
    return pool

docs.title: 3. Structure Sets
docs.text:
The Structure Set ties everything together. It defines the generation rules (biomes, spacing) and the starting point.

from anvil.api.world.structures import JigsawStructureSet
from anvil.api.vanilla.biomes import MinecraftBiomeTags
from anvil.api.core.filters import Filter

def generate_dungeon():
    # 1. Initialize pools
    start = dungeon_start_pool()
    rooms_pool()

    # 2. Create the set
    # one structure per 10x10 chunk cell, kept 4 chunks from the cell edge
    dungeon_set = JigsawStructureSet("my_dungeon", separation=4, spacing=10)

    # 3. Add the main structure configuration
    main_structure = dungeon_set.add_jigsaw_structure(
        "my_dungeon_structure",
        start_pool=start,            # Start with this pool
        max_depth=4,                 # How far out to branch
        start_height=30,             # Y level (underground)
        placement_step="underground_structures",
        start_height_from_sea=False,
    )

    # 4. Add Biome Filters
    main_structure.add_biome_filters(
        Filter.any_of(
            [
                Filter.has_biome_tag(MinecraftBiomeTags.Plains),
                Filter.has_biome_tag(MinecraftBiomeTags.Forest),
            ]
        )
    )

    # 5. Queue everything
    for pool in pools:
        pool.queue()
    dungeon_set.queue()

docs.title: Full Workflow
docs.text:
1. Design in Game: Build your structures and save them with Jigsaw blocks.
    • Set the Target Pool in Jigsaw blocks to match your pool names (e.g., my_namespace:dungeon_rooms).
    • Save .mcstructure files to assets/structures/<category>/<name>.mcstructure.
  2. Define in Python: Use the code above to register your pools and sets.
  3. Run: Anvil will export the structure set, which the game uses to generate your dungeon.

Linking Pools

In your Jigsaw Block inside Minecraft: - Target Pool: my_namespace:dungeon_rooms (matches JigsawStructureTemplatePool("dungeon_rooms") + implicit namespace) - Name: connector_a (matches the name you connect to) - Target Name: connector_a (connection point on the other piece)

docs.title: Wearables and Attachables
docs.text:
This tutorial makes an Iron Crown: a helmet item with durability, enchantability and repair, rendered on the player's head by an attachable. The attachable is the item's client and uses the same API as an entity client.

Every snippet compiles as written.

docs.title: The Item
docs.text:
items/iron_crown.py
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel.enums import EnchantsSlots, ItemCategory, ItemGroups, Slots
from anvil.api.items.components import (
    ItemDurability,
    ItemEnchantable,
    ItemIcon,
    ItemRarity,
    ItemRepairable,
    ItemWearable,
)
from anvil.api.items.items import Item
from anvil.api.pbr.texture_set import TextureComponents
from anvil.api.vanilla.items import MinecraftItemTypes

item = Item("iron_crown")
item.server.description.set_menu_category(ItemCategory.Equipment, ItemGroups.Helmet)
item.server.components.add(
    ItemIcon(textures=TextureComponents(color="iron_crown")),
    ItemWearable(slot=Slots.Head, protection=2),
    ItemDurability(max_durability=180),
    ItemEnchantable(slot=EnchantsSlots.ArmorHead, value=10),
    ItemRepairable().add_repair_item(
        items=[MinecraftItemTypes.IronIngot()],
        repair_amount="context.other->query.remaining_durability + 45",
    ),
    ItemRarity(value="rare"),
)

"components": {
  "minecraft:icon": {"textures": {"default": "tut:iron_crown"}},
  "minecraft:wearable": {"slot": "slot.armor.head", "protection": 2},
  "minecraft:durability": {"max_durability": 180},
  "minecraft:enchantable": {"slot": "armor_head", "value": 10},
  "minecraft:repairable": {"repair_items": [{"items": ["minecraft:iron_ingot"], "repair_amount": "context.other->query.remaining_durability + 45"}]},
  "minecraft:rarity": "rare",
  "minecraft:display_name": {"value": "item.tut:iron_crown.name"}
}
  • ItemWearable(slot=Slots.Head) makes the item equippable; Slots.Chest, Slots.Legs, Slots.Feet, Slots.Body and Slots.Offhand are the others. protection is the armor value.
  • ItemEnchantable uses the enchantment slot names (EnchantsSlots.ArmorHead, Sword, Bow...).
  • repair_amount can be a number or Molang.

docs.title: The Attachable
docs.text:
attachable
client = item.client.description
client.add_geometry("iron_crown")
client.add_texture("iron_crown", TextureComponents(color="iron_crown"))
client.animation("iron_crown", "offset", animate=True)
client.render_controller("default").set_geometry("iron_crown").add_texture(
    "iron_crown"
)

item.queue()

"minecraft:attachable": {
  "description": {
    "identifier": "tut:iron_crown",
    "materials": {"default": "entity_alphatest"},
    "textures": {"iron_crown": "textures/tut/tutorial/actors/iron_crown/iron_crown"},
    "geometry": {"iron_crown": "geometry.tut.iron_crown"},
    "animations": {"offset": "animation.tut.iron_crown.offset"},
    "scripts": {"animate": ["offset"]},
    "render_controllers": ["controller.render.tut.iron_crown.default"]
  }
}

Model and animation

Build the crown in Blockbench on the player's head bone, so it follows the head. The offset animation is how the model is positioned when worn; it is also where first-person and third-person differences go, with Query.IsFirstPerson() conditions, as in Adding a Custom Item.

Hiding the vanilla armor

When the attachable replaces an armor piece, add a material such as client.add_material("default", "armor") and use the vanilla armor render controller behaviour: client.render_controller("default").set_geometry(...) with part visibility tied to Query.IsItemNameAny(...).

docs.title: Full Example — Iron Crown
docs.text:
items/iron_crown.py
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel.enums import EnchantsSlots, ItemCategory, ItemGroups, Slots
from anvil.api.items.components import (
    ItemDurability,
    ItemEnchantable,
    ItemIcon,
    ItemRarity,
    ItemRepairable,
    ItemWearable,
)
from anvil.api.items.items import Item
from anvil.api.pbr.texture_set import TextureComponents
from anvil.api.vanilla.items import MinecraftItemTypes


def iron_crown():
    item = Item("iron_crown")
    item.server.description.set_menu_category(ItemCategory.Equipment, ItemGroups.Helmet)
    item.server.components.add(
        ItemIcon(textures=TextureComponents(color="iron_crown")),
        ItemWearable(slot=Slots.Head, protection=2),
        ItemDurability(max_durability=180),
        ItemEnchantable(slot=EnchantsSlots.ArmorHead, value=10),
        ItemRepairable().add_repair_item(
            items=[MinecraftItemTypes.IronIngot()],
            repair_amount="context.other->query.remaining_durability + 45",
        ),
        ItemRarity(value="rare"),
    )

    client = item.client.description
    client.add_geometry("iron_crown")
    client.add_texture("iron_crown", TextureComponents(color="iron_crown"))
    client.animation("iron_crown", "offset", animate=True)
    client.render_controller("default").set_geometry("iron_crown").add_texture(
        "iron_crown"
    )

    item.queue()
    return item


IronCrown = iron_crown()

docs.title: Generating Features
docs.text:
This tutorial fills the Ember Fields biome from Creating a biome with an ore, scattered lanterns and trees. World generation has two halves: a feature describes what to place, and a feature rule describes where and how often. Scatter features sit in between to repeat another feature.

Every snippet compiles as written.

docs.title: Ore
docs.text:
worldgen/ember_features.py
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel.enums import FeatureRulePlacementPass
from anvil.api.core.filters import Filter
from anvil.api.features.feature import CoordinateRange
from anvil.api.features.feature_rule import FeatureRule
from anvil.api.features.ore import OreFeature
from anvil.api.vanilla.blocks import MinecraftBlockTypes

in_ember_fields = Filter.has_biome_tag("ember_fields")

ore = OreFeature("ember_ore", count=9, discard_chance_on_air_exposure=0.3)
ore.add_replace_rule(
    MinecraftBlockTypes.Magma(),
    [MinecraftBlockTypes.Basalt(), MinecraftBlockTypes.Blackstone()],
)
ore.queue()
FeatureRule("ember_ore", ore, FeatureRulePlacementPass.UndergroundPass).biome_filter(
    in_ember_fields
).distribution(
    iterations=12,
    scatter_chance=None,
    x=CoordinateRange("uniform", (0, 16)),
    y=CoordinateRange("uniform", (-20, 40)),
    z=CoordinateRange("uniform", (0, 16)),
).queue()

"minecraft:feature_rules": {
  "description": {"identifier": "tut:ember_ore", "places_feature": "tut:ember_ore"},
  "conditions": {"placement_pass": "underground_pass", "minecraft:biome_filter": {"test": "has_biome_tag", "value": "ember_fields"}},
  "distribution": {
    "iterations": 12,
    "x": {"distribution": "uniform", "extent": [0, 16]},
    "y": {"distribution": "uniform", "extent": [-20, 40]},
    "z": {"distribution": "uniform", "extent": [0, 16]}
  }
}
  • OreFeature(name, count) places a vein of count blocks; each replace rule says which block is placed into which blocks.
  • FeatureRule(name, feature, placement_pass) runs the feature per chunk. distribution(iterations, scatter_chance, x, y, z) says how many tries and where: a number, a Molang string or a CoordinateRange(distribution, extent).
  • A biome filter is a Filter, the same ones spawn rules use.

docs.title: Scattered Blocks
docs.text:
A single-block feature places one block with attachment rules. A scatter feature repeats it, and the feature rule places the scatter.

lanterns
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel.enums import BlockFaceValues
from anvil.api.features.scatter import ScatterFeature
from anvil.api.features.single_block import SingleBlockFeature

lantern = SingleBlockFeature("ember_lantern", enforce_placement_rules=True)
lantern.place_block("tut:brass_lantern")
lantern.may_attach_to(
    BlockFaceValues.Down, [MinecraftBlockTypes.Basalt(), MinecraftBlockTypes.Blackstone()]
)
lantern.queue()

lanterns = ScatterFeature("ember_lanterns", lantern, project_input_to_floor=True)
lanterns.distribution(
    iterations=3,
    scatter_chance=(1, 6),
    x=CoordinateRange("uniform", (0, 16)),
    y=64,
    z=CoordinateRange("uniform", (0, 16)),
)
lanterns.queue()
FeatureRule(
    "ember_lanterns", lanterns, FeatureRulePlacementPass.SurfacePass
).biome_filter(in_ember_fields).distribution(
    iterations=1, scatter_chance=None, x=0, y="query.heightmap(0, 0)", z=0
).queue()

"minecraft:scatter_feature": {
  "description": {"identifier": "tut:ember_lanterns"},
  "places_feature": "tut:ember_lantern",
  "project_input_to_floor": true,
  "distribution": {
    "iterations": 3,
    "scatter_chance": {"numerator": 1, "denominator": 6},
    "x": {"distribution": "uniform", "extent": [0, 16]},
    "y": 64,
    "z": {"distribution": "uniform", "extent": [0, 16]}
  }
}

Note

scatter_chance is a percentage, a (numerator, denominator) fraction or a Molang string; None means always. project_input_to_floor drops the scatter's start position to the ground, so the lanterns land on the surface wherever y=64 was.

Custom blocks in features

A feature takes your blocks as "namespace:name" strings or as block.descriptor(lit=True) with state values.

docs.title: Trees
docs.text:
trees
from anvil.api.features.tree import TreeFeature
from anvil.api.vanilla.biomes import MinecraftBiomeTags

tree = TreeFeature("ashen_tree")
tree.base_block(MinecraftBlockTypes.Dirt())
tree.may_grow_on([MinecraftBlockTypes.Basalt(), MinecraftBlockTypes.Dirt()])
tree.trunk(MinecraftBlockTypes.DarkOakLog(), trunk_height=(5, 9))
tree.spruce_canopy(MinecraftBlockTypes.DarkOakLeaves(), max_radius=(2, 4))
tree.queue()
FeatureRule("ashen_trees", tree, FeatureRulePlacementPass.SurfacePass).biome_filter(
    Filter.all_of([in_ember_fields, Filter.has_biome_tag(MinecraftBiomeTags.Overworld)])
).distribution(
    iterations=2,
    scatter_chance=(1, 4),
    x=CoordinateRange("uniform", (0, 16)),
    y="query.heightmap(variable.x, variable.z)",
    z=CoordinateRange("uniform", (0, 16)),
).queue()

A tree is one trunk builder (trunk, fancy_trunk, mega_trunk, cherry_trunk, mangrove_trunk...) plus one canopy builder (canopy, spruce_canopy, fancy_canopy, mega_pine_canopy...), with optional trunk_decoration, canopy_decoration and mangrove_roots.

Other features

anvil.api.features also has AggregateFeature (several features at one spot), SequenceFeature, WeightedRandomFeature, SearchFeature, GeodeFeature, VegetationPatchFeature, StructureTemplateFeature and more; they combine the same way. Jigsaw structures are in Using Jigsaw.

docs.title: Full Example
docs.text:
worldgen/ember_features.py
from anvil.lib.jsonmodel.enums import BlockFaceValues, FeatureRulePlacementPass
from anvil.api.core.filters import Filter
from anvil.api.features.feature import CoordinateRange
from anvil.api.features.feature_rule import FeatureRule
from anvil.api.features.ore import OreFeature
from anvil.api.features.scatter import ScatterFeature
from anvil.api.features.single_block import SingleBlockFeature
from anvil.api.features.tree import TreeFeature
from anvil.api.vanilla.biomes import MinecraftBiomeTags
from anvil.api.vanilla.blocks import MinecraftBlockTypes


def ember_features():
    in_ember_fields = Filter.has_biome_tag("ember_fields")

    ore = OreFeature("ember_ore", count=9, discard_chance_on_air_exposure=0.3)
    ore.add_replace_rule(
        MinecraftBlockTypes.Magma(),
        [MinecraftBlockTypes.Basalt(), MinecraftBlockTypes.Blackstone()],
    )
    ore.queue()
    FeatureRule("ember_ore", ore, FeatureRulePlacementPass.UndergroundPass).biome_filter(
        in_ember_fields
    ).distribution(
        iterations=12,
        scatter_chance=None,
        x=CoordinateRange("uniform", (0, 16)),
        y=CoordinateRange("uniform", (-20, 40)),
        z=CoordinateRange("uniform", (0, 16)),
    ).queue()

    lantern = SingleBlockFeature("ember_lantern", enforce_placement_rules=True)
    lantern.place_block("tut:brass_lantern")
    lantern.may_attach_to(
        BlockFaceValues.Down, [MinecraftBlockTypes.Basalt(), MinecraftBlockTypes.Blackstone()]
    )
    lantern.queue()

    lanterns = ScatterFeature("ember_lanterns", lantern, project_input_to_floor=True)
    lanterns.distribution(
        iterations=3,
        scatter_chance=(1, 6),
        x=CoordinateRange("uniform", (0, 16)),
        y=64,
        z=CoordinateRange("uniform", (0, 16)),
    )
    lanterns.queue()
    FeatureRule(
        "ember_lanterns", lanterns, FeatureRulePlacementPass.SurfacePass
    ).biome_filter(in_ember_fields).distribution(
        iterations=1, scatter_chance=None, x=0, y="query.heightmap(0, 0)", z=0
    ).queue()

    tree = TreeFeature("ashen_tree")
    tree.base_block(MinecraftBlockTypes.Dirt())
    tree.may_grow_on([MinecraftBlockTypes.Basalt(), MinecraftBlockTypes.Dirt()])
    tree.trunk(MinecraftBlockTypes.DarkOakLog(), trunk_height=(5, 9))
    tree.spruce_canopy(MinecraftBlockTypes.DarkOakLeaves(), max_radius=(2, 4))
    tree.queue()
    FeatureRule("ashen_trees", tree, FeatureRulePlacementPass.SurfacePass).biome_filter(
        Filter.all_of([in_ember_fields, Filter.has_biome_tag(MinecraftBiomeTags.Overworld)])
    ).distribution(
        iterations=2,
        scatter_chance=(1, 4),
        x=CoordinateRange("uniform", (0, 16)),
        y="query.heightmap(variable.x, variable.z)",
        z=CoordinateRange("uniform", (0, 16)),
    ).queue()


ember_features()

docs.title: Kit
docs.text:
anvil.kit holds ready-made content built on top of the API: call one function and get a complete, working feature such as a full wood set.

Stability

The kit is opinionated and may change between minor versions of Anvil: names, parameters and the content it generates can all change. Pin your Anvil version if you depend on a kit's exact output.

The API (anvil.api) is the stable layer. If you need full control or long-term stability, build on the API directly and use the kit as a reference.

docs.title: Optional dependencies
docs.text:
Some kits need packages that a plain pip install mcanvil doesn't include. Install them through the matching extra:

Kit Extra Install anvil.kit.world.ldtk ldtk (Amulet) pip install mcanvil[ldtk]

Importing a kit without its extra raises an ImportError naming the command to run.

docs.title: Blocks
docs.text:
• anvil.kit.blocks.wood_set: a complete wood set (planks, logs, wood, slabs, stairs, fences, gates, doors, trapdoors, buttons, pressure plates, signs (standing and wall in one block), hanging signs, boats and chest boats) with recipes, vanilla wood tags, fuel values, creative inventory placement and the TypeScript components they need.
from anvil.kit.blocks.wood_set import WoodBlock, create_wood_set

create_wood_set("rotten", tree=my_tree)                      # everything; saplings grow `my_tree`
create_wood_set("rotten", WoodBlock.SAPLING)                 # everything but saplings: no tree needed
create_wood_set("rotten", WoodBlock.DOOR, tree=my_tree)      # everything but doors
create_wood_set("rotten", own_creative_group=True, tree=my_tree)  # in its own creative group
create_wood_set("rotten", map_color="#5C4A32", tree=my_tree)  # the color of every block on maps

WoodSet("rotten").sound_group(BlockSoundGroup.Mud)             # a vanilla sound group, for all parts
WoodSet("rotten").options(WoodBlock.DOOR, open_sound="rotten.door_open")  # a sound a script plays

wood = create_wood_set("rotten", tree=my_tree)
block, item = wood["planks"]                                # each part is a (block, item) pair

A set with saplings needs tree, the feature they grow into (a Feature, its identifier, or a function that builds it from the finished set: tree=lambda wood: make_tree(wood["log"].block, wood["leaves"].block)); the kit makes no trees. Build and queue it yourself: it can use the set's blocks by their identifiers (<namespace>:<name>_log, <namespace>:<name>_leaves with its natural state on).

docs.title: World
docs.text:
• anvil.kit.world.potionsAPI: potion variants (drinkable, splash, lingering) and brewing recipes.
  • anvil.kit.world.ldtk: builds a Minecraft world from an LDtk map. Needs the ldtk extra.

docs.title: Actors
docs.text:
• anvil.kit.actors.components: a custom projectile item component.
  • anvil.kit.actors.materials: an entity outline material.

docs.title: The WoodSet class
docs.text:
create_wood_set covers the simple case. For anything more, build the set with the class:

palm = (
    WoodSet("palm", exclude=WoodBlock.CHEST_BOAT)
    .tree(lambda wood: make_palm(wood["log"].block, wood["leaves"].block))
    .leaf_drop(coconut, 0.02)  # drops when the leaves are broken (no shears) or decay
    .build()
)
palm["planks"].block
  • tree is a feature, its identifier, or a function receiving the set once its blocks exist. Once built, palm.tree_feature is the resolved feature.
  • leaf_drop(item, chance, count=1) takes an Item or an identifier like minecraft:apple.
